item.title: Broadcom denied names of cloud providers backing VMware merger challenge
item.description: Euro cloud trade association CISPE can keep the identities of members backing its VMware merger challenge confidential from Broadcom following a ruling by the EU General Court. Cloud Infrastructure Services Providers in Europe filed an action last year seeking to annul the European Commission's approval of Broadcom's acquisition of the cloud and virtualization giant. CISPE believes the Commission erred in allowing the purchase to go ahead without imposing any conditions on Broadcom to protect the many European cloud providers and their customers who depend on VMware's software. Broadcom sought access to redacted information identifying members supporting the action, arguing that it needed the information to challenge the action's admissibility. CISPE says the ruling allows the case to proceed without disclosing those identities to Broadcom. "It is a procedural ruling on confidentiality rather than a decision on the substance of the case, but it removes the immediate obstacle to the action moving forward," a CISPE spokesperson told The Register . CISPE argued that identifying the members, which are or have been VMware customers, would expose them to a significant risk of retaliation because of Broadcom's market power. Those members had supplied information about their commercial relationships with VMware. As far as the case itself goes, CISPE says it warned the Commission that Broadcom would use VMware's pre-eminent position in the private cloud market to rewrite licensing terms and reshape the market in its favor. Just a month after Broadcom's acquisition concluded in November 2023, partners were informed that VMware's channel program was to end in early 2024, and that Broadcom was also ditching the majority of VMware's Cloud Services Providers , keeping only a select few that had the largest turnover. Despite Broadcom CEO Hock Tan publicly stating that inflating prices was not his strategy, that is what happened. AT&T says that Broadcom proposed a 1,050 percent price increase , for example. Meanwhile, nine out of ten respondents to a recent survey of VMware customers said they were considering moving to alternatives. CISPE, which represents 48 cloud infrastructure service providers across the EU, says fewer than 20 European providers remain authorized to offer VMware-based services, down from more than a thousand. Commenting on the latest ruling, CISPE Secretary General Francisco Mingorance declared it a good day for the organization and for the rule of law in Europe. "The case matters even more today than when we filed it. In the three years since the European Commission waved this deal through without conditions, Broadcom has dismantled the European VMware channel ," he said . "Those excluded have until 31 March, 2027, to sell their infrastructure or their customers to a competitor chosen by Broadcom, or to close. This is the foreclosure the European Commission was warned about." We asked CISPE what outcome it hoped to achieve, nearly three ye

item.title: Why does Betelgeuse keep fading? The mystery of Orion's giant star
item.description: null Betelguese, one of the brightest stars in the night sky, has been putting on quite a show lately — but not in the way you might expect. The famous red supergiant in the constellation Orion has been growing noticeably fainter in recent months. Of the 21 brightest stars in the night sky, Betelgeuse is perhaps the most enigmatic. Its changing brightness poses a puzzle: how do the star's pulsations, dust eruptions, and a possible companion contribute to its fading? A giant star with a puzzling name Even the translation of Betelgeuse's name is contentious. For a long time, it was thought to be a corruption of three Arabic words, usually translated as "The Armpit of the Giant." However, other experts in star nomenclature now dispute that interpretation, proposing instead "The Hand of al-Jauzā," with al-Jauzā referring to Orion. Although classified as a red supergiant, Betelgeuse usually appears more orange than red— golden orange or deep topaz. It is one of the most famous stars in its class. Henry M. Neely (1877-1963), for many years a popular lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium , described its restless behavior in his book A Primer for Stargazers : "(Betelgeuse) expands and contracts spasmodically, like an old man with his strength almost entirely spent, panting in the asthmatic decrepitude of old age." The rhythms of a changing star Betelgeuse naturally expands and contracts like a beating heart. As an aging red supergiant, it has a regular pulsation cycle of roughly 430 days: when it expands, its outer layers cool and it dims; when it contracts, they heat up and it brightens. Among first-magnitude stars — the brightest category of stars in the night sky — it is the only marked variable. Its scale is equally remarkable: located 650 light-years away, Betelgeuse is among the largest and most luminous stars of its class, with a luminosity of about 14,000 suns at maximum and 7,600 suns at minimum. Only a few such objects have been identified in our galaxy. British astronomer Sir John Herschel (1792-1871) first noticed Betelgeuse's variability beginning in 1836. Astronomers describe apparent brightness using magnitude : lower numbers mean brighter stars. In April 2023, Betelgeuse reached magnitude 0.0 — as bright as Vega , the fifth brightest star. At minimum brightness, such as in 1927 and 1941, its magnitude may fall to +1.2, making it appear about three times fainter. Three threads run through this mystery: Betelgeuse's roughly 430-day pulsation, its much longer recurring dimming cycle, and the exceptional Great Dimming of 2019—2020. Keeping them, separate helps explain why one cause need not account for every change in brightness. Betelgeuse shines in the constellation Orion. (Image credit: Franco Tognarini via Getty Images) A longer cycle and a possible companion Alongside its roughly 430-day pulsation, Betelgeuse shows a mysterious 2,100-day (5.75-year) dimming cycle. item.title: Dozens killed, dozens more missing after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site
item.description: The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people. Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post. FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

item.title: Nigerians will choose the best product in the marketplace – Obi Media to Governors
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The media office of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, Peter Obi, has taken a swipe at the state governors, accusing them of pushing to undermine democracy, warning that any election that falls short of being free, fair and transparent will fail. The Peter Obi Media Office, POMR noted that it had become aware of a series of covert attempts by governors to interfere with the democratic process, just as it cautioned that Nigerians would resist any process that did not meet the required standards of free, fair and transparent elections. In a statement signed on Tuesday by the POMR spokesman, Idris Zekeri, he reminded the governors that, despite their alleged fraudulent efforts, they were presenting a poor product and that Nigerians would choose the best option available in the marketplace. Buy Maps Zekeri condemned what it described as the increasing desperation of the governors, who, it said, were turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging instead of presenting their records of service, performance and achievements. According to the office, Nigerians had had enough and remained determined to reject undeserving leaders who had failed them, adding that the 2027 election would be a defining moment for the country and that Nigerians were resolved to reclaim their country through the power of their votes. The statement also said Peter Obi remained the people’s preferred choice because he embodied the strongest offering in the political arena: a leader defined by competence, capacity, character, compassion and commitment, capable of raising Nigeria from its current condition and restoring its dignity, prosperity and hope. The statement read, “The Peter Obi Media Office has become aware of a series of covert efforts by state governors to undermine the democratic process. It once again cautions that any process that falls short of free, fair, and transparent elections will fail, as Nigerians will resist it. “The Media Office reminds the governors that, regardless of their fraudulent efforts, they are presenting a poor product, and Nigerians will select the best option available in the market. “We therefore condemn the increasing desperation of these governors, who, instead of presenting their records of service, performance, and achievements, are turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging. “Leadership is a privilege earned through service; it is not a mandate to retain power through deceit, intimidation, or interference with the democratic process. “Nigerians have had enough and remain determined to reject undeserving leaders who have failed them. The 2027 election will be a defining moment for our nation. item.title: Akron men's basketball opens 2026-27 season with win, Zips women lose
item.description: The University of Akron basketball teams opened their 2026-27 seasons Monday, Nov. 2, with the men winning and the women losing. Returnee Evan Mahaffey started and newcomer Kamrin Oriol entered as a reserve in Akron 's 75-61 men's basketball win over host Louisiana in a Mid-American Conference-Sun Belt Challenge game in the Cajundome in Lafayette. The eligibility of Mahaffey and Oriol has been in question, but both played in an exhibition win over Youngstown State University on Oct. 27 and an Oct. 29 order filed by the Ohio Supreme Court kept them available to play by preserving a previous ruling made earlier in October. Ty Pence leads Akron men's basketball to win in Dustin Ford's debut as head coach Ty Pence totaled 19 points, eight rebounds and two assists in his Akron debut as Dustin Ford won his first game as Zips men's basketball head coach. Pence, who previously played at Illinois State, made 6 of 12 shots from the field, including 2 of 7 from beyond the 3-point arc, and 5 of 5 free throws in 34 minutes. Akron newcomer Tahj Staveskie scored 16 points and had three assists in 38 minutes. Mahaffey contributed 16 points, 11 rebounds and three assists in 33 minutes. Akron scored the first eight points and never trailed. Zips newcomer Colin White made a 3-pointer and Pence added two layups and a free throw in the opening 8-0 run. Akron led 46-29 at halftime. White finished with nine points and four rebounds. Oriol totaled five points, six rebounds and three assists. Returnee Halil "Chabi" Barre and newcomer Buddy Hammer Jr. each had four points and four rebounds. Louisiana's Jamyron Keller scored a game-high 26 points and had four assists. Dani Pounds scored 15 points and Trent Middleton Jr. added 14 points. Akron women's basketball team falls in season opener by one point The Akron women's basketball team lost its season opener 75-74 to visiting South Alabama at Rhodes Arena. Kailee Bransford made a 3-pointer to give Akron a 74-73 lead with 23 seconds left in the game, but Jaida Redwine made a layup with less than two seconds left to lift South Alabama to victory. Akron newcomer Macey Fegan, who previously played at Cleveland State, recorded a double-double with 17 points and 12 rebounds in 31 minutes. Akron's Shaena Brew had 12 points and four assists. Tyla Heard contributed 10 points, seven rebounds, three assists and three steals. Bransford and Monique Mitchell each scored nine points. Jessie Joaquim added eight points and 11 rebounds. CJ Wilson led South Alabama with 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Jolie Mantz scored 16 points, Julieta Ceja scored 12 points and Deborah Orianegbena had nine points and 12 rebounds. Michael Beaven can be reached by email at mbeaven@thebeaconjournal . This article originally appeared on Akron Beacon Journal: Akron men's basketball opens 2026-27 season with win, Zips women lose

item.title: Pauldo 'Twin Backcourt' celebrates NJ return with Rutgers hoops
item.description: PISCATAWAY — Mia Pauldo could hear it every time she touched the basketball. The high-pitched cheers started, "Mia! Mia!" from the top corner of the lower bowl of Jersey Mike's Arena. Her twin sister Mya Pauldo heard the same thing. It was their support system from Paterson, reminding them why they came home. Mia and Mya Pauldo helped Rutgers polish off Long Island University, 83-52, in the season opener. With their family and dozens of kids behind them, the twins began to put their disappointing freshman seasons behind them. "I was locked in for sure, but I love when they're loud and obnoxious," said Mia, the Scarlet Knights' point guard, who had 21 points, seven rebounds and five assists. "It reminds me why I do what I do. They definitely know who we are. Paterson kids are so awesome." Rebuilding Rutgers basketball The last time Mia and Mya Pauldo walked off the court at Jersey Mike's Arena after a meaningful game, they raised their third straight NJSIAA championship trophy with Morris Catholic. The "Twin Backcourt" was at the University of Tennessee last winter, where Mia Pauldo earned a starting role. The former McDonald's All-American and three-time Morris County Player of the Year averaged 10.4 points – best by a Vols freshman since 2017-18 – 2.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 23.3 minutes, and was named to the All-SEC Freshman team. The Pauldo twins were part of a mass exodus from Knoxville, where all eight potential returning players opted for the transfer portal. They committed to Rutgers and new head coach Gary Redus II 12 days later. "We've got three good players from Jersey here, and we want to keep bringing them back home," said Redus, who has six home-state players on the Rutgers roster. "That has to be a staple for us to be successful." THE TWIN BACKCOURT BACK IN ACTION IN JERSEYYYY 🤩 #GoRU | #RUWBB pic.twitter.com/RifSglyTzI — Rutgers Women’s Basketball (@RutgersWBB) November 3, 2026 Mya Pauldo was named Most Valuable Player as Rutgers won gold at the FISU American Games in Lima, Peru in July. She averaged 12.2 points in the five-game tournament, scoring 16 against Argentina in the final. "Us coming back here, it feels the same. It's a full circle moment," said Mya, who had six points, five rebounds and three assists. "We're just playing at a higher level. ... It was Coach Gary having confidence in me and my sister playing together. Coming back to Jersey was a perfect situation. We play better with our people here. We are what we are today because of them." Morris Catholic coach Rahim Huland El brought the girls basketball team to the season opener on Nov. 2, seated directly in front of the Pauldos' four grandparents. The twins' father, D.J. Pauldo, was also a vocal presence as usual. He and several family members have Rutgers season tickets. It's a big change from 10-hour drives to Knoxville. item.title: Liverpool could have the next Trent Alexander-Arnold already lined up
item.description: Liverpool could have the next Trent Alexander-Arnold already lined up Lenix Conde Could Be Liverpool’s Long-Term Right-Back Answer After Ronald Araujo Impact There is something old-fashioned about Ronald Araujo. Liverpool supporters take to players who make the game look like it matters, and the Uruguayan has done exactly that. According to Anfield Watch, he has turned early doubt into real affection at Anfield, and it is not hard to see why. The original report says, “Araujo has become a fan favourite. He’s someone to adore. Someone to really look up to because of the way he plays with such fervent passion and enthusiasm.” That rings true. Supporters can forgive a lot when a player throws himself into the fight, wins duels and treats every loose ball like a personal insult. IMAGO Araujo making right-back role his own What has surprised many is where he has done his best work. The assumption was that he would arrive as a centre-back option, especially with Jeremy Jacquet “settled so seamlessly”. Instead, Andoni Iraola found another use for him. “Andoni Iraola started to trial him as a right-back and the switch worked,” the report states, and that feels like an understatement. There is a practical logic to it. With Jeremie Frimpong carrying “his current niggle” and Conor Bradley still recovering from a long-term injury, a door opened. Araujo walked straight through it. The report adds, “He has since made the role his own.” In the short term, that makes perfect sense. He is aggressive, competitive and reliable in the defensive moments that matter. Lenix Conde emerging as Liverpool right-back prospect Yet football never stops moving. The same piece points to the next chapter, and it is an intriguing one. “Liverpool need someone a bit more dynamic. Someone capable of being defensively solid and offer creativity in attack.” That is the challenge with Araujo. He can lock down a flank, but he is “not a natural right-back” and “offensively, he cannot give Iraola what he wants.” Enter Lenix Conde. Anfield Watch describes him as “the best right-back Liverpool have produced since Trent Alexander-Arnold” and says the 18-year-old is “now starting to catch the eye for the Reds’ U18 side.” Those are big words, but they speak to the profile Liverpool will want in that role over time, someone “composed on the ball, capable of making forward runs and just very sound defensively”. Pathway opening for English wonderkid The important thing here is not to force the issue too soon. Young players need room to grow. Still, the path is visible. If Conde continues on “the same trajectory”, then the idea that he could replace Araujo in the years ahead is not fantasy, it is planning. Iraola will surely look at the position with a hard, clear eye. For now, Araujo gives Liverpool steel. In the future, Conde may offer the balance every top side craves, bite at the back, quality on the ball and the courage to keep going forward. Our View This is the sort of report that gets the

item.title: Californians vote on billionaire tax to replace federal cuts in healthcare funding
item.description: California could become the first US state to tax the net worth of billionaires Tuesday under a ballot measure that has divided liberal leaders nationally and triggered one of the most expensive ballot fights in state history as the ultra-rich scramble to figure out whether they would pay the tax or flee. Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

item.title: Unclear what comes next as US strikes Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The United States on Monday attacked Iran's Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, even as President Donald Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict. The Journal, citing unnamed US officials, described the strike against Qeshm, the the largest island in the Strait of Hormuz, as the latest of a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks.

item.title: Spanish footballer De Miguel dies after collision with keeper
item.description: Jesus De Miguel was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball (Gabriel BOUYS) Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match. "Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 am (7am GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," his club Tenerife said in a statement. "No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news." De Miguel, 30, was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball. The incident happened towards the end of the match at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, with the teams level at 2-2. Owono was sent off and the match was subsequently abandoned. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically", before his death. "I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media. Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" to De Miguel's family, team-mates and Tenerife. Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish football federation (RFEF). "Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today," wrote the federation in a statement. The RFEF postponed Tuesday's matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina, "as a gesture of respect and solidarity". Real Madrid held a minute of silence before their training session on Tuesday. La Liga side Espanyol also delayed the presentation of their new coach Eder Sarabia to Wednesday. De Miguel had been at Tenerife for just over a season, having joined in the summer of 2025 from Castellon. The striker helped the team gain promotion to the second division. The forward began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023. gr-rbs/bc

item.title: Jaissle admits Newcastle players abandoned the game plan in Everton defeat
item.description: Jaissle admits Newcastle players abandoned the game plan in Everton defeat Matthias Jaissle admitted Newcastle United failed to carry out their game plan in the 1-0 defeat to Everton and says his side were not brave enough. The Newcastle boss was particularly frustrated by how little his team were able to involve striker Will Osula, with too many long balls played towards the striker. “We could not bring him into situations,” Jaissle said. “We need to jump the first lines with clear patterns on how we want to play football. Just playing long balls is for sure not the style he prefers. “And it was not the plan; that is something you clearly need to mention. “This is now the next step to clearly analyse it in-depth, and ask why we could not start the game as we originally planned.” Jaissle said the frustration inside the dressing room matched that of the supporters after a performance which failed to reflect what he had seen in training. “I was aware of that and it was the same in the locker room,” he said. “Big frustration, big disappointment, because we couldn’t transfer what we saw during the week, a team training on a high level in the approach of how we actually wanted to play and then since the referee started the game, not much was seen and that’s difficult to understand. “Of course the fans are frustrated like we are.” The Newcastle boss also felt his midfield failed to provide enough support in helping the team play through Everton’s press. “We played with a double six today that should support our centre-backs, also to break the first line,” Jaissle said. “We couldn’t bring them in the game. We were not brave enough, not courageous enough to break that line and to play on the ground as well, and finding our patterns on the pitch. “It looked really good in the training session but almost nothing to see of these aspects during the game.” Jaissle added that Newcastle also lacked conviction in the final third. “We were not brave enough to really go all the way to make the last steps and force them to make mistakes,” he said. “Also in possession, it was not the plan to shoot the long balls. We spoke about patterns and how we can create problems, create two vs one situations on the pitch, but again it was not much to see today in these 90 minutes and it’s something we need to work on.”

item.title: Michelle Gisin, two-time Olympic Alpine skiing gold medalist, retires
item.description: Michelle Gisin, who won the final two Olympic gold medals in Alpine skiing's individual combined event in 2018 and 2022, announced her retirement at age 32. Gisin missed the 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics after tearing knee ligaments and sustaining injuries to her spine and wrist in a downhill training crash last December. Deciding to retire "was a long process that took place alongside my rehabilitation, but also in the years leading up to it," she said, according to a translation of a Swiss Ski Team press release . "When I returned to St. Moritz in September, I felt a great deal of gratitude — for my health, but above all for all the wonderful moments I've been fortunate enough to experience throughout my long career. ... It took a little while for my mind to catch up with my heart. But now I'm very happy and looking forward to everything the future holds for me.” Gisin leaves ski racing as the last woman to win Olympic gold in the individual combined event, which was replaced on the program after 2022 with a team combined event. She also took super-G bronze in 2022, plus world championships medals in the combined in 2017 (silver) and 2021 (bronze). She won one individual World Cup race -- a slalom in 2020 -- among 21 individual World Cup podiums. Her first Olympic gold in 2018 came four years after older sister Dominique shared downhill gold with Slovenian Tina Maze. “It was a wonderful time – and I truly appreciate that I was able to enjoy it so much," Michelle Gisin said, according to the release. "Now I’m incredibly excited to finally be able to do what I’ve missed all these years: ski, on the slopes of my own choosing.” How to watch FIS Alpine skiing World Cup during 2026-27 season; broadcast schedule The World Cup season begins Oct. 24-25 in Soelden, Austria. item.title: Personal Style Is Alive and Well. Just Ask Ifeoma Odogwu #LagosFashionWeek2026
item.description: From runway shows to intimate presentations and the week’s most stylish gatherings, the fashion editor and creative consultant made a case for directional dressing with oodles of personality. Ifeoma Odogwu , better known as Hyperfashun , is easily one of the best dressed women in Lagos, and arguably on the continent and per usual her Lagos Fashion Week style is peerless. A familiar face in Nigeria’s fashion industry, the former Genevieve Magazine fashion editor, stylist to stars such as Toke Makinwa and more, the creative consultant has spent years working with designers, discovering emerging talent and helping shape the visual language of Nigerian fashion. So, naturally, when Lagos Fashion Week comes around, we’re just as interested in what she’s wearing as we are in what she’s watching. From the bustling Lagos Fashion Week tents at Federal Palace Hotel to a packed calendar of offsite presentations and fashion events across the city, Odogwu embraced the occasion with a wardrobe that made getting dressed part of the experience. At the tents, she joined the fashion crowd for presentations by Y’Wande , NYA The Label , E.S.O by Liman and FIA Factory , taking in some of the exciting design talent shaping the season. But as anyone familiar with Lagos Fashion Week knows, the shows have evolved. Some of the week’s most interesting moments happen elsewhere, and Odogwu’s itinerary reflected just how much the city’s fashion calendar has expanded. She made the rounds at presentations by Jewel Jemila , The Ladymaker, Rendoll, Kilentar, Onalaja and Orange Culture , and made time for the social side of fashion week, too, including the Made By Us pop-up at Melrose Loft and Tiffany Amber’s Breakfast Club. What makes Odogwu particularly interesting to watch is the perspective she brings to personal style. As someone whose career has been built around fashion imagery, designers and creative expression, her wardrobe offers another way of engaging with the industry she’s helped champion. Ifeoma has a certain clarity in her style and an unmatched point of view, something that’s often lacking in the sameness of our Instagram-driven world. Her style reminds us that what makes personal style compelling is individuality, curiosity and a willingness to have fun with fashion. Scroll through for a closer look at Ifeoma Odogwu’s Lagos Fashion Week wardrobe, from the runway tents to the events around town. Ifeoma Odogwu/Instagram Romantic vibes in @jeweljemila . Happy to be back in Lagos for another exciting season of @lagosfashionweekofficial . Day 1 of prancing around included the Jewel Jemilia anniversary show, then made a dash before the doors at @atafo__ closed, then to @ejiroamostafiri and finally ended at the official Heineken and Lagos fashion week press cocktail. item.title: NFL analyst labels the Dallas Cowboys ‘a joke’ after loss to the Cardinals in Week 8
item.description: Photo by Elsa/Getty Images After suffering their fifth loss in eight games, a former NFL star has ruthlessly called the entire organisation out for their terrible performances. The Dallas Cowboys are struggling once again this season after a 3-5 start to the year. Many fans were hoping that this is the year it would all click for Dallas, but they have suffered some frankly embarrassing defeats. The latest one was a 33-30 loss against the Arizona Cardinals. Dallas has played down to opposition endlessly during this NFL campaign so far. Losses against the Buccaneers and the Packers were ample evidence of that. And one analyst has had enough of the Cowboys, going on an epic rant and letting the organisation know exactly what is wrong with them. Damien Harris claims everyone involved with the Dallas Cowboys, from the quarterback to the owner is a ‘joke’ In the game against the Cardinals, the Cowboys gave up a two-score lead in the fourth quarter, allowing 20 points in the final period of play. The offence wasn’t able to keep up with Arizona either, and it eventually led to the narrow defeat. After the game, Damien Harris in the studio ripped into the franchise, calling out Prescott in particular. “The Cowboys are a joke,” Harris said. “This team, this organisation, the quarterback, the head coach, everybody. It is a joke. Not only to mention that this was supposed to be the greatest show on turf. Not only did they give a 14-point halftime lead, they gave up a 24-10 fourth quarter lead. “They allowed over 500 yards of offence to Gardner Minshew, and the combination with Jacoby Brissett. For Dak Prescott… This is a guy who deserves to be in the MVP conversation… It’s time for us to start making Dak Prescott to take accountability. Where is the leadership? Where is the ownership on this football team? This team plays like they’ve already been eliminated from the playoffs.” While it may come off as a bit harsh for Harris to say all this, it would be difficult for Prescott and the Cowboys to deny it as well. Dallas needs to get it together if they are going to achieve anything this year, but it’s likelier that they won’t do anything of note in the Dak era overall. item.title: Pirates prospect update: Pair of young Bucs excelling in Arizona Fall League
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates sent nine of their prospects to the Arizona Fall League, but there’s been two that have stood out above the rest of their counterparts. Wyatt Sanford has returned to form with the Glendale Desert Dogs, and has picked up where he left off after his season with Greensboro was cut short due to injury. Sanford ended up playing in 72 games for the Grasshoppers, and had a great second season of professional baseball. The 20-year old shortstop bulked up a little bit from last year and in the process nearly quadrupled his home run totals. With Glendale Sanford continues to show that the power he brought to Greensboro was not a fluke. He has left no doubt in the eyes of viewers and scouts that he’s currently the best Pirates hitter in the AFL. The Frisco native currently has a slash line of .291/.400/.436 with two homers, nine RBIs and one stolen base. On October 22, Sanford smashed a 454 foot home run. On the pitching side of things, the surprise star of this group has been Bryan Mena. The 22-year old righty is not currently listed in the Pirates’ top 30 prospects list, but he has far in a way been the best pitching prospect from Pittsburgh’s system in the AFL. Although he had an average season with Greensboro, he’s playing some of his best baseball with the Desert Dogs as of late. 454 feet ⚡️ Wyatt Sanford ( @Pirates ) puts a charge into his second home run of the @MLBazFallLeague campaign: pic.twitter.com/wEIpm1IYr9 — MLB Pipeline (@MLBPipeline) October 23, 2026 In his stint in Arizona, Mena has not given up a single earned run in four contests with the Desert Dogs. Mena’s most recent outing saw him appear for 2.2 of relief for Glendale. He gave up three hits and a walk, while striking out five batters in the 1-0 win over Salt River on Oct. Overall Mena has pitched 27.7⅔ scoreless innings (two starts) and has recorded 11 strikeouts, allowed just 3 walks, has a 1.57 WHIP and has limited opposing hitters to a .273 opponent batting average. Time will tell if this kind of showcase makes him a prime candidate for Pittsburgh’s bullpen in the future. The AFL regular season concludes on November 11, and although Glendale has the worst record, the Pirates’ prospects represented on the team will have several more opportunities to showcase their abilities amongst the best minor league players in the league.

item.title: West Ham talk to Parker after sacking boss Nuno
item.description: Nuno Espirito Santo took charge of West Ham in September 2025 [Shutterstock] West Ham United have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo after their disappointing start to the Championship season. The 52-year-old has been in charge since September 2025 and oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season. BBC Sport understands that the club are in advanced talks with former Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham boss Scott Parker as his replacement. Former England midfielder Parker had four seasons as a player with the Hammers and led Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship as a manager. Nuno is out - who next for West Ham? What happens now at relegated West Ham? Widely seen as favourites for automatic promotion, the London side are currently eighth in the table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough. They have won two of their last six games and have lost back-to-back home matches - going down 3-2 to Southampton and then 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday - losses that have seen them drop down from second place. Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left the club. Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of the side for their Championship trip to Cardiff City on Wednesday night. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club's objectives and expectations remain on track," a West Ham United statement read. "West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the club, and wish them all the very best for the future. "The process of recruiting a new head coach is already under way." Nuno Espirito Santo's last win as West Ham boss came at Swansea City [Shutterstock] The decision means West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent manager since David Moyes left London Stadium in May 2024. His successor Julen Lopetegui was sacked after just six months in charge with the Hammers mid-table having won six of their 20 Premier League matches. He was replaced by former Chelsea and Brighton boss Graham Potter, who oversaw a 14th-placed finish, but was sacked after only eight months in charge with the club 19th in the table. The club opted to stick with former Wolves and Tottenham Hotspur boss Nuno despite him being unable to turn around the club's fortunes. They were relegated at the end of last season after finishing two points behind Spurs. Despite that, this season had a troubled start for the Hammers - they failed to win any of their first three league matches and were 19th in the table. A run of four successive wins in the first half of September, where they scored 16 goals and went top of the table, appeared to show they had adapted to the second tier, with a 6-0 win over Wrexham the highlight of the run. item.title: Nuno Espírito Santo is sacked as former Newcastle star set to take over at West Ham
item.description: Nuno Espirito Santo bubbles Nuno Espírito Santo has been sacked by West Ham. An official club statement on Tuesday morning revealing the news. Nuno Espírito Santo sacked with West Ham sitting eighth in the Championship, six points behind league leaders Middlesbrough and the Hammers only two points off third. The official club statement beginning: ‘West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect. Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.’ Nuno Espírito Santo managed just over 13 months with the Hammers, having arrived late September 2025. The official West Ham statement going on to say: ‘Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed. West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future. The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway. Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of squad preparations ahead of tomorrow evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City, and the Club will make no further comment until the appointment of the new Head Coach is confirmed.’ David Ornstein at The Athletic has reported that former Newcastle United star Scott Parker has already agreed to take over at West Ham. Parker also played for the Hammers back in the day.

item.title: Barcelona set clear conditions for Pedro Porro transfer as Tottenham’s demand emerge
item.description: Barcelona set clear conditions for Pedro Porro transfer as Tottenham’s demand emerge It is known that Barcelona are interested in signing Tottenham Hotspur defender Pedro Porro , but any transfer will depend on the Spanish international securing more favourable departure conditions from the Premier League club. According to SPORT , the Catalan side admire the 27-year-old, with Hansi Flick and the sporting department both approving his profile, but are unwilling to meet Tottenham’s current €70 million valuation . The outlet mentions that Barcelona have already made contact with the defender’s representatives, who believe his time in English football could be approaching an end. As mentioned by the player himself, Porro is keen on returning to Spain and views the possibility of joining Barcelona favourably. However, financial considerations remain the biggest obstacle to completing a deal, particularly with the club prioritising other positions in the transfer market. Barcelona interested in Porro after previous transfer discussions Pedro Porro wants to return to Spain. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Porro has been on Barcelona’s radar since last summer, when the club explored the possibility of strengthening their right-back position. The first discussions were dependent on Barcelona generating funds through a major defensive departure. Both Alejandro Balde and Jules Kounde were considered potential candidates to leave, but neither ultimately moved on, forcing the club to put the Porro operation on hold. Real Madrid had also been linked with the Tottenham defender, although that possibility has lost momentum because of the competition for places in their right-back department. Tottenham’s €70 million valuation creates major obstacle Barcelona have Pedro Porro on their radar. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) The biggest complication is Tottenham’s financial demands, with the London club valuing Porro at approximately €70 million, a figure Barcelona consider excessive and beyond their current willingness to spend. The Catalan hierarchy have therefore made their position clear to the player’s representatives. They want Porro to become directly involved in facilitating a transfer by helping establish a considerably more realistic asking price. Tottenham’s reputation for driving hard bargains further complicates negotiations, and without a significant reduction in their demands, Barcelona are unlikely to pursue the operation, particularly during the January window.

item.title: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm island – Report
item.description: The United States launched limited strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, US media reported, as Iranian media reported five explosions in quick succession. The reported strikes came as US voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump’s grip on power. The strikes, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, hit Qeshm Island, strategically located in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets. Unnamed US officials cited by the Journal, CNN, The New York Times and several other outlets, described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes. It also said they had not been publicly announced to avoid the impression Washington intended to resume major combat operations. US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment. The US and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months. Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokespeson told AFP, “No”. Israel also held an election last week that saw Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party come out on top, but still short of a majority. The reported attack came just hours after Trump signaled a deal with Iran “could happen”, as American voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought. “Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. It did not say what was behind the explosions. – Ball in US court – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, said indirect negotiations were taking place with the US. “Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi told state media. On Tuesday, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has been Tehran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, said that while Iran was ready for war it had given Washington a “rational response”. “The ball is now in America’s court to prevent war.” Oil prices had plunged by more than seven percent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict. – Reopen the strait – US Vice President JD Vance said both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement. “We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” Vance told reporters on Monday. China also called for a return to diplomacy, while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Last week, the Axios news outlet reported that Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new ta

item.title: Isack Hadjar blames himself for George Russell clash that “ruined” his Mexico GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Isack Hadjar has taken some responsibility for his collision with George Russell at Formula 1’s Mexico GP, in which he miraculously scored two points. Hadjar qualified down in seventh at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, two tenths and three spots away from Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen , but gained two positions courtesy of a decent start. The Frenchman was holding off Russell, but the Mercedes racer still kept his front tyres alongside Hadjar’s rear wheels instead of backing out going into Turn 6, sending the Red Bull into a spin. “It's a shame,” Hadjar said. “I honestly did not expect George to stick a wheel up Turn 6, because the corner was completely mine. I was aware of him, and I shouldn't have trusted him in the end, but it happens. Clearly, it's a shame, it's completely ruined my race. “To me, honestly, it's my fault if that happened today, the lap-one incident. If I had done a better job yesterday, I wouldn't be starting seventh, maybe we are fighting for better than a podium and we don't meet George on the way. These things happen, but it's better to maximise your chance at the front. I should have done a better job.” Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing, spins Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing, spins Russell, who skipped post-race media duties and therefore did not weigh in on the incident, copped a 10-second penalty, while Hadjar found himself down in 22nd, with “little damages on the floor”. Other than the struggling Aston Martins, he was the first driver to pit, on lap seven. “Pace on the medium on the first stint, any time I had free air, was good,” he said. “When we pitted for the soft, I only did two laps [before the safety car and red flag], but I felt super quick. During that lap one, I was like ‘OK, I have a shot for the podium’, and then it was finished.” Following his first tyre change, Hadjar successively overtook Valtteri Bottas , Ryo Hirakawa, Carlos Sainz and Sergio Perez . He was unlucky to pit shortly before the safety car and red flag; further moves on Sainz, Nico Hulkenberg , Perez and Alex Albon brought him up to 12th only, as he struggled to fight his way through the field. “Everyone has SM mode [straight mode],” he explained. “It's just a train of cars and there's no way to really overtake. I really struggled. I even had a great fight with Checo. He was very late on the brakes in the straight, I wasn't really catching up. It was terribly hard. Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing “In the end, it's not like Mexico used to be a track where you could overtake [previously]. With the temperatures, the altitude, everything is on fire once you're following someone.” Speaking before penalties were announced for Oscar Piastri , Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto – meaning he inherited ninth place after all – Hadjar could only see one positive from the race. item.title: Draymond Green forgets his own ‘therapy’ advice as Warriors star gets ejected vs. Suns
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Veteran forward Draymond Green had a forgettable night during the Golden State Warriors’ latest matchup against the Phoenix Suns. The Golden State Warriors walked away with a 116-113 win over the Phoenix Suns in a nail-biting game during the NBA regular season. It was the Stephen Curry show, who finished the night with 34 points, 6 rebounds, and 7 assists in 33 minutes of playing time. Unfortunately, the biggest talking point from the game became Draymond Green’s viral altercation with Suns’ Dillon Brooks and Khaman Malauch, which led to the Warriors star’s ejection. Draymond Green’s ‘therapy’ message falls flat after ejection vs. Phoenix Suns Over the years, Green has built a reputation of letting his emotions get the better of him, which often leads to ejections and fines for the Warriors veteran. However, just days before the Warriors vs. Suns game, Green spoke up about how some NBA players should attend therapy sessions to keep their emotions in check. Well, it seems Green should have listened to himself, as he failed to follow his own advice against the Suns. “It does because ultimately it helps your temperament. It helps you in decision-making. It helps you in patience. It helps you have grace. “And so I think ultimately it does because it makes you a better person,” Green said . He added, “And being a better person is 1,000% going to make you a better player because it affects all the other things that you do. It affects your whole being.” The only silver lining for the 4x NBA champion was that the Dubs still ended up with a win and have now improved to a 5-3 record for the season. item.title: Antonelli chooses Hamilton route over following Verstappen and Norris
item.description: Kimi Antonelli has made his decision to continue racing with '12' in Formula 1 next season and will not take over '1' from McLaren's Lando Norris.” Antonelli became the youngest-ever world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix, where he finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. Antonelli is following the same approach as Hamilton. For next season, the Mercedes driver could have chosen to race with '1' as his number, but he will stick with '12' instead. Hamilton also kept '44' despite winning multiple world championships, while Verstappen and Norris both chose to race with '1'. Antonelli commented after the race: "I think I'll stay with number 12. I'll stay with number 12 because, obviously, it's a very special number for me, but also it's a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble, and I feel like by keeping number 12 it allows me to have a new point where to start and build on everything again and try to improve. "And also, to be honest, I'm very superstitious, and number one has never been a good number for me. Whenever I put it, it went extremely badly. So one more reason to stay with number 12. But, yeah, I will stay with number 12." Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen and Hamilton praise Antonelli Verstappen explained he is proud of the young Italian driver. He said: "Well, I think to achieve this in your second year in Formula 1 is always very impressive. Because, of course, at his age as well, to be so solid, not make big mistakes, and, of course, also beat your experienced teammate, he's just driven incredible. "And I'm very proud of him, how he has handled himself this whole season. It's not always easy to deliver every single weekend, but he has done that, and he's the deserved champion this year." Hamilton added: "It was beautiful to be up there with these two and to be up there with Kimi for his first World Championship. I think it was a very special moment, one of the most special moments that I remember having here."

item.title: Kentucky is drunk on football. Will Stein has made winning intoxicating
item.description: Matt Jones’ experience hosting Kentucky Sports Radio told him to expect a few calls or texts about Kentucky basketball on his Monday morning show after UK’s first exhibition game. Basketball never sleeps in Kentucky. It did, however, take a backseat on KSR’s airwaves that day. Jones was 37 minutes deep into his show before anyone mentioned basketball. Jones, his cohosts, and the show’s callers and texters had football on the brain. “It’s intoxicating,” Jones said on the airwaves that day. College football’s biggest weekend yet? Ranking Week 10's stacked slate of must-see games For two hours, the conversation fixated on Will Stein’s surging football team that, at the time, was fresh off a win against Oklahoma . Blue blood became another pelt on the wall for the Big Blue. Now, that’s worth discussing. “On that Monday’s show, it would’ve normally been maybe half football and half basketball, but there was like five minutes (of conversation) on basketball,” Jones told USA TODAY Sports. “All anybody wanted to talk about was football. I’ve never seen it like that.” ‘Never seen the city like this.’ You’d need to be a fan of a certain age to remember a Kentucky season quite like this one. Kentucky is 7-1 for the first time since 1977. It’s ranked No. 7 in the US LBM Coaches Poll entering a rivalry game at No. 16 Tennessee. Kentucky’s strength of record ranks No. 2 in the nation behind only undefeated Miami, according to ESPN metrics. When you consider the resume, you’d be entitled to believe Kentucky would be ranked higher if not for its name and its history. “How do you go earn respect? Go win. That’s it,” Stein told USA TODAY Sports. “And, soon, people will respect this program.” Buoyed by an overtime win against LSU, Kentucky would possess a compelling playoff resume if it wins at least three of its final four games. Kentucky is finding out what Indiana already experienced: A state crazy about basketball can fall in love with a winning football program. “I’ve never seen the city like this, in terms of cheering on the football team like they are right now,” senior safety Ty Bryant told USA TODAY Sports. Bryant is something of an authority on this subject. He's a Lexington, Kentucky, native who previously played for Mark Stoops. “It just makes me want to continue doing what we’re doing,” Bryant said of the fanbase's energy. “We have to continue to give them something to cheer about.” It’s not that Kentucky’s never tasted success. Bear Bryant once served an 11-1 season. Fran Curci’s Wildcats finished 10-1 in 1977. Stoops twice delivered 10-win seasons. Each time, the success proved fleeting. A lack of consistency became Kentucky's bugaboo. So, is this sustainable? Ask Stein or his boss that question, and you’ll detect nothing but belief. “It’s completely possible that we can have elite-level football on an annual basis here, that we are in the hunt for championships,” athletic director J Batt told USA TODAY Sports. “That is the goal. item.title: As Yankees free agency begins, we rank their 5 best targets for 2027
item.description: A year ago, the Yankees had one clear free agent target in Cody Bellinger. But the lefty-hitting, Gold Glove left fielder lingered on the market until Jan. 21, when he agreed to a five-year, $162.5 million contract. That deal contains an opt out after the 2027 season, the start of which could be affected by a work stoppage. MLB’s current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, and a looming lockout will impact business over the next four weeks. With free agency now underway, here’s a ranking of five potential Yankees targets: 5. Luis Arraez Position: Second base, first base In his recent assessment of the Yankees’ latest early October exit, owner Hal Steinbrenner pointed to an inconsistent offense. “Some of them just underperformed,’’ said Steinbrenner “They didn’t live up to what they’re capable of.’’ This year’s Rays-Brewers World Series, won by Milwaukee, featured lineups that routinely put the ball in play and pressure an opponent’s defense. And in this year’s free agent class, lefty-hitting Luis Arraez is a connoisseur of contact, with just 28 strikeouts in 655 plate appearances in 2026, while batting .310 for the Giants and Phillies . A three-time batting champ, Arraez – who turns 30 in April – came up with Minnesota in 2019, with James Rowson, then the Twins batting coach. But Rowson’s immediate future as Yanks’ batting coach is cloudy and Arraez’s complete lack of power and shaky defensive reputation (though he improved his metrics as a second baseman this year) are marks against a long-term deal. 4. Paul Blackburn Position: Relief pitcher Yes, the bullpen is a volatile area. Blackburn’s success in 2026 doesn’t guarantee a repeat in 2027 and 2028. But the right-hander was such a revelation – at a bargain price – that a multi-year contract must be a consideration. Like the Luke Weaver path, Blackburn transformed from a shaky starter to a trusted and valuable multi-inning reliever in pinstripes. Blackburn added depth to his sinker, increased his changeup use, and posted a 1.69 ERA in 62 appearances during his free agent walk year. Given the uncertainty about Fernando Cruz’s partially torn UCL, a reunion with Blackburn should be on the Yanks’ winter list. 3. Adrian Morejon Position : Relief pitcher Or the Yankees could make a higher priority of this setup lefty. Morejon’s durable profile and high-octane arsenal could create a competitive market among contenders seeking both elite multi-inning relievers and closers. Over the past three seasons in San Diego, Morejon has averaged 70 appearances, and a 2.58 ERA with 10 strikeouts and 0.4 home runs allowed per nine innings. With the swing-and-miss ability from his sinker/slider/changeup/four-seam fastball mix is an elite groundball rate (58 percent this year). Given Brent Headrick’s overuse in a breakout season, the Yanks could use another significant lefty bullpen presence. 2. item.title: Mee and Kenny handed first Northern Ireland call-ups
item.description: Dermot Mee and Eoin Kenny are both underage internationals with Northern Ireland [Getty Images] Manchester United goalkeeper Dermot Mee and Portsmouth forward Eoin Kenny have been handed their first Northern Ireland call-ups for November's final Nations League matches with Ukraine and Hungary. Mee, 23, is a former Northern Ireland underage international and, although he has not played competitively for United this season, will add competition to NI's first choice goalkeeper Pierce Charles. Wide player Kenny, who is the son of former Republic of Ireland manager Stephen, joined Portsmouth from Dundalk in July. The 20-year-old has made one league appearance for the Championship club, but has been handed a first call up as Dion Charles, Eoin Toal and goalkeeper Bailey Peacock-Farrell drop out of the squad. Sunderland defender Dan Ballard is missing after he injured his hamstring in the September win over Georgia in Tbilisi, while midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell are also absent through injury. Liverpool's Conor Bradley, who has not played since January, remains a long-term absentee. Family affair at Croke Park caps Mee's special night Michael O'Neill's side are unbeaten at the top of League B2 and can earn promotion to the top tier for the first time. Northern Ireland face Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday, 14 November at 19:45 GMT before they travel to Hungary in their final match on 17 November. Both games are live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds. Northern Ireland are the only side left in the entire Nations League who have yet to concede a goal in this year's competition. Shea Charles scored a last-gasp winner in Georgia in September before a goalless draw at home to Hungary. A 3-0 victory over Ukraine was one of the most impressive performances from O'Neill's young side, and they ended the quadruple-header with another goalless draw, this time at home to Georgia. If Northern Ireland can top the group they would not only win promotion to League A, but they would also be all but guaranteed of a play-off for Euro 2028. Northern Ireland squad Goalkeeper : Pierce Charles (QPR - on loan from Manchester City), Conor Hazard (Wycombe Wanderers), Dermot Mee (Manchester United) Defenders : Trai Hume (Sunderland), Tom Atcheson (Blackburn Rovers), Ciaron Brown (Oxford United), Ruairi McConville (Norwich City), Paddy McNair (Hull City), Terry Devlin (Portsmouth), Brodie Spencer (Oxford United), Michael Forbes (Dundee) Midfielders : Shea Charles (Fulham), Ethan Galbraith (Stoke City), Kieran Morrison (Sheffield Wednesday - on loan from Liverpool), Paul Smyth (QPR), Isaac Price (West Brom), Justin Devenny (Stoke City), Jordan Thompson (Preston North End) Forwards : Jamie Donley (Luton Town - on loan from Spurs), Ceadach O'Neill (Arsenal), Eoin Kenny (Portsmouth), Josh Magennis (Stevenage), Callum Marshall (Luton Town), Braiden Graham (Everton).

item.title: England scrum-halves Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland ruled out of Australia clash
item.description: Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland have been ruled out of Sunday’s autumn opener against Australia in an escalation of the disruption faced by England at half-back. With first-choice fly-half Fin Smith engaged in a race against time to recover from a calf strain in time for the Wallabies’ visit to Allianz Stadium, England have been forced to rule scrum-halves Mitchell and McParland out of contention. Mitchell damaged his hamstring when on Northampton Saints duty against Gloucester on Saturday and is to undergo a scan, placing his involvement in the second phase of the Nations Championship in doubt. McParland missed the 28-14 victory at Franklin’s Gardens because of a calf issue sustained during England’s training camp last week and it is hoped he will recover in time to face Japan or New Zealand later in the month. For exclusive stories and all the detailed rugby news you need, subscribe to The Rugby Paper website, digital edition, or newspaper from as little as 14p a day. INJURED: Northampton Saints’ Archie McParland will England’s clash with Australia. PICTURE: Joe Giddens/PA Replacements for missing scrum-halves To fill the vacancies created in his 36-man squad, head coach Steve Borthwick has called up Ben Spencer and Harry Randall. Spencer is just three games into his comeback from shoulder surgery for Bath , but appeared as a replacement in the climax to England’s July tour against Argentina, while Randall has been an ever-present for Bristol Bears so far this season. Both players are competing to provide support to Leicester Tigers ‘ Jack van Poortvliet, who reclaimed the number nine jersey during the summer and would have been competing with Mitchell for the starting role against Australia. With Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Seb Atkinson having proved their fitness from respective hamstring and knee problems by starting for Exeter Chiefs and Gloucester, they have been promoted into the squad. As a result, Noah Caluori and Max Ojomoh drop out of the 36-man group that is to gather at England’s Surrey training base on Monday evening. CONCERN: Alex Mitchell’s involvement in England’s autumn is in doubt because of a hamstring injury. PICTURE Ben Whitley/PA Fin Smith fitness race Smith is being given until Wednesday to demonstrate he can pull the strings in the Ella Mobbs Trophy showdown with George Ford, Marcus Smith and Charlie Atkinson the alternatives if he is ruled out. There is one change to the forwards named a week ago because of the withdrawal of rookie hooker Kepueli Tuipulotu due to a knee injury incurred during last week’s three-day training camp. Theo Dan comes in as his replacement and will add depth in the position behind Jamie George and Luke Cowan-Dickie. item.title: NFL fans react to Bears proving Monday Night Countdown crew’s Seahawks prediction wrong
item.description: Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images The Chicago Bears proved the likes of Pat McAfee and Jason Kelce wrong when they beat the Seattle Seahawks on Monday. The Seahawks’ form has declined a great deal since their success last year and they have now lost more games this season (4) than they did in the entirety of 2025/26 (3). Their latest defeat came at the hands of the Bears on Monday, losing 34-17 despite several of the Monday Night Countdown crew backing them to pick up the victory. NFL on ESPN shared an image of the predictions prior to the game, which included McAfee going for a 27-21 win and Kelce also picking the Seahawks to come out on top (27-24). Fans have since come back to the post after the result to share their reactions. One wrote: “Those picks didn’t age well huh?? When are you going to start to Bear down peeps.” Another stated: “Didn’t Caleb teach you guys last week?!” A third commented : “They didn’t age well,” with another writing: “I expected more from you here @PatMcAfeeShow, Spears the only one that knows ball apparently.” Several fans also replied post-game to write ‘Update?’ in response, while another fan tweeted: “Wrong again. Except for Spears.” The Seahawks will now be aiming to bounce back this weekend against the Arizona Cardinals who are 3-5. Read more: NFL fans had a lot to say after fireworks crash into a helicopter during Seahawks vs Bears game ‘On his way’: Skip Bayless makes a mid-game prediction about Caleb Williams during Seahawks vs Bears ‘Who got fleeced?’ – Bears fans celebrate as Jeffery Simmons debut highlight goes viral

item.title: Flyers Game 17: Lines, Notes, & How to Watch vs. Wild
item.description: The Philadelphia Flyers (4-8-4) are home for one last game before a 5-game road trip on Tuesday, when they host the Minnesota Wild (10-3-3) at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Puck drop is at 7:00 PM ET. The Flyers enter Tuesday’s game after a dominating 6-3 win over the Utah Mammoth in the return of Owen Tippett and Travis Konecny. Konecny was a standout in the win, with 3 of the 4 forward lines finding the scoresheet, and Jamie Drysdale having a career-high 3-point and +5 game. The Wild come into Philly on a 5-game point streak, winning 4 of their last 5 games, and picking up points in 8 of their last 9 games. They have the 3rd most standings points in the league through 16 games. Puck drop is at 7:00 PM ET at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Here is everything you need to know before the game. Read More: Flyers Postgame Blog: Konecny’s Return & What Went Right Flyers Projected Lines & Pairs vs. Wild Forwards Trevor Zegras – Christian Dvorak – Travis Konecny Tyson Foerster – Denver Barkey – Owen Tippett Porter Martone – Noah Cates – Matvei Michkov Cole Knuble – Sean Couturier – Noel Acciari Defensemen Travis Sanheim – Jamie Drysdale Cam York – Oliver Bonk Nick Seeler – Simon Benoit Goalies Dan Vladar Joseph Woll Special Teams PP1: Drysdale, Zegras, Barkey, Martone, Michkov PP2: Bonk, Dvorak, Foerster, Tippett, Konecny PK1: Couturier, Dvorak, York, Sanheim PK2: Cates, Foerster, Drysdale, Seeler Notes Tuesday is expected to be forward Bobby Brink’s first game against his former team, the Flyers, since being traded. At the last deadline, Brink was traded to Minnesota in a one-for-one swap, sending defenseman David Jiricek to the Flyers. Brink was banged up the one time the Flyers traveled to Minnesota last season after the trade, so not only will this be his first trip to Philadelphia, but it will also be his first game against the Flyers. He deserves a tribute video. The Flyers will also have a ton to build on from their Sunday win against the Mammoth. They were playing much like the team that had a bunch of success during the 2025-26 season. The Flyers were getting back to their pesky ways, forechecking hard, forcing mistakes, and taking advantage of those mistakes. Minnesota will provide just as tough a matchup as Utah, but with better goaltending. Can the Flyers keep up? To add to that, the Wild are 7th in the league with 52 goals for this season. They’re allowed the 4th fewest goals in the league with 36. The team that Bill Guerin has assembled in Minnesota is going to be a challenge. Rick Tocchet spoke about getting one of Dan Vladar or Joseph Woll into a more traditional top goalie role, and ditching the every-other-game rotation. With Vladar playing extremely well, and Woll struggling a bit in his last few starts, could Tuesday be the day Vladar gets two in a row? I think it’s the smart move, but we’ll know for sure after Tocchet’s morning media availability on Tuesday. How to Watch Flyers vs. Wild TV: NBC Sports Philadelphia, ESPN+ (Out-of-Market Stream) Radio

item.title: Live Sports Coming to Algorithm-Driven Feeds on Discovery Platforms
item.description: Live Sports Coming to Algorithm-Driven Feeds on Discovery Platforms It’s been well reported that TikTok streamed select live sporting events, including player-focused MLS alt feeds and portions of FIFA World Cup matches, earlier this year. But over the last 90 days, the short-form video platform has quietly started to include full, primary event broadcasts within users’ feeds. “The same algorithmic feed that created countless new celebrities & consumer businesses is now coming for live content. This is beyond disruptive,” former MVP Chief Strategy Officer Mitch Glaser said. Jake Paul’s Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) billed its August 21 card featuring Amanda Serrano vs. Lucrecia Manzur as the first championship boxing production to air live on TikTok. “We gave them the full show––the main event, everything. [And] it performed incredibly well because the TikTok community discovered our broadcast by simply scrolling their main feed,” Glaser said. “Over 100m impressions and incredible engagement amongst a demo that was 68% under the age of 35.” It’s believed the experience will prompt TikTok to add more live sporting events and that other social discovery platforms could follow suit, potentially creating several new distributional channels for rights owners. “TikTok is seeing platform benefits to having professionally generated content in their live product,” Glaser said. “Eventually, I would expect that Instagram, X and YouTube will lean in more as well.” The Next Era of Sports Innovation From ESPN's first Super Bowl to immersive fan experiences and the next era of content creation, the 6th Annual ESPN Edge Innovation Conference explores the technology and ideas transforming sports. Join leaders across sports, technology and business for an evening of conversations on innovation, storytelling and the future of the fan experience. Watch Live, Free and Open to All November 12 | 5–7 p.m. ET Featuring ESPN Edge innovation partners Accenture, Microsoft, Meta, and WSC Sports. Learn more! TikTok’s move to include live premium IP within a user’s personalized ‘for you’ content feed is a noteworthy media development. For the first time, someone on the platform “will be scrolling like normal and land in a live sports broadcast,” Glaser said. “This changes streaming [on] social platforms from easy to access and free to view to easy to access, free to view and highly discoverable.” And games and events airing on TikTok now have the potential to ‘go viral’ while they’re still live. “If the stream is performing well, if the content is engaging, it's going to go up the algorithmic ranking and appear in more users’ feeds,” Glaser said. That is meaningfully different from how users discover content on Instagram (IG) or YouTube (YT). On IG, only live streams from accounts users follow appear at the top of their feeds, while YT viewers generally must seek out live video programming themselves. “People are overlooking how powerful this is because people have streamed t

item.title: Rio Ferdinand expects Saliba to still get his Arsenal shirt back
item.description: Rio Ferdinand expects Saliba to still get his Arsenal shirt back William Saliba has been sidelined since the start of the season , with Arsenal allowing him time to recover from a longstanding back problem. The club opted against surgery and instead gave the defender time to rest and regain his fitness. He last played competitive football at the World Cup and missed Arsenal’s pre-season preparations. However, the Gunners have coped with his absence, helped by the summer arrival of Ezri Konsa . The Englishman has impressed alongside Gabriel, with the pair developing a strong partnership in central defence. Nevertheless, Saliba remains a world-class talent, and his return will give Mikel Arteta an important selection decision. Saliba’s return presents Arteta with a dilemma Saliba is back in training and nearing a return, although Arsenal will want to ensure he has recovered fully before bringing him back into action. Konsa has done enough to deserve his place, but Saliba is also too talented to leave on the bench. Arteta may therefore need to find a way to accommodate both defenders without disrupting the partnership that has served the team well. Rio Ferdinand believes Saliba’s quality means the manager will find room for him, and suggested Konsa could move to right back. William Saliba (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Ferdinand discusses Arsenal’s defensive options Speaking via Metro Sport , Ferdinand praised both players and explained why he expects Saliba to return to the starting team. ‘I think William Saliba is one of those guys that you have to find room for in the team. ‘He’s that good, he’s top. ‘I said to my son yesterday, “watch Ezri Konsa”, because everything he does is efficient. That’s a great problem for Mikel Arteta to have. ‘I wouldn’t be surprised if Konsa goes back to right-back once Saliba comes back. I wouldn’t be surprised because Konsa is top.’ Saliba’s return will give Arteta more defensive options, but he must manage the defender’s recovery carefully. If the Frenchman is ready to play, Konsa’s versatility could allow both players to remain important to Arsenal. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow….
