item.title: Di Gregorio set to remain in the Premier League beyond January
item.description: Di Gregorio set to remain in the Premier League beyond January Michele Di Gregorio is unlikely to leave Bournemouth during the January transfer window, despite previously being linked with a move to Bologna . The Serie A club had reportedly considered bringing the goalkeeper back to Italy, but their interest appears to have cooled in recent weeks. Di Gregorio joined the Premier League side at the start of this season on loan after Luciano Spalletti made it clear that he would not be Juventus’ first choice between the posts. The decision left the goalkeeper looking for an opportunity elsewhere, and Bournemouth offered him the chance to continue his career in England. His situation has not been straightforward, however, as he has mostly featured in cup competitions since arriving at the Cherries. Despite limited opportunities, he has continued working hard in training and remains determined to earn more minutes. Bologna interest appears to have faded Bologna were reportedly interested in signing Di Gregorio in January because they wanted to make him their first-choice goalkeeper. A return to Serie A could have offered him a clearer route to regular football, particularly given his current role at Bournemouth. However, according to Tuttomercatoweb , that possibility is now unlikely after the Italian side cooled their interest over recent weeks. The report indicates that Di Gregorio is expected to remain in England and complete his loan spell with Bournemouth this season. That development means the goalkeeper will have to continue competing for opportunities at his current club. Although he has not yet established himself as their number one, his commitment and performances have reportedly been appreciated by the club. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Bournemouth could make his move permanent The Cherries are said to be satisfied with Di Gregorio’s contributions so far and could look to turn his loan into a permanent transfer. Such a decision would represent a show of confidence in the goalkeeper, even though he has not yet secured a regular starting position. A permanent move could also give him greater stability as he attempts to establish himself in English football. Rather than having to consider another change of club after the current campaign, he would have the opportunity to focus on earning the trust of the coaching staff.

item.title: Tuesday ‘Dawg Bites Is Ready To Turn The Page… Almost.
item.description: ATHENS, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 17: Georgia Bulldogs mascot Uga XI is seen on the field during the game between the Auburn Tigers and Georgia Bulldogs at Sanford Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Athens, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Tuesday, Bulldog fans! Your Georgia Bulldogs have played two-thirds of their regular season games, and two-thirds of their SEC conference games. And, two-thirds of the “traditional” rivals on the schedule, with only Georgia Tech left in a few weeks. Are you still basking in the glow of a freshly flambe ’ ed gator? You should be. We have 360+ days to remind booger-eaters who still runs our state and theirs. Lots of other folks were impressed with the Bulldog defense that stymied the previously 4th-ranked SEC offense. That includes the folks in Birmingham, who awarded Chris Cole the SEC Defensive Player of the Week, and Gabe Harris the SEC Defensive Lineman of the Week. The initial College Football Playoff rankings will be revealed tonight on ESPN at 7:00 pm ET. Georgia may well be #2, just as it is in the AP poll, with Miami at #1. The real drama will be surrounding teams like 2-loss Ohio State, who are obviously not as good without injured QB Julian Sayin. The same could be said for Wake Forest, whose only loss was to the #1 Hurricanes, but with a QB who left Saturday’s game early. Utah is undefeated and starting to steamroll opponents. UCLA likewise undefeated but with a fairly weak schedule. Kentucky with some of that new car smell. What does the committee think of Indiana, with a very close loss to Ohio State but also winning by the skin of their teeth most weeks thanks to Cignetti’s deal with the devil? Notre Dame lost to BYU but has otherwise looked very good vs. weaker competition, and BYU is also sitting with one loss – I sincerely hope, and solely for my own entertainment, to have BYU ahead of the Whinin’ Irish. Coach Kirby Smart held his weekly Monday press conference, and I have to say he was a little more verbose on topics such as tampering and in-season roster management, SEC scheduling as it relates to night games in Athens vs. on the road, and motivation of players in the era of NIL. I don’t think there are any soundbites worthy of national scrutiny (unlike his post-WLCOP comments regarding injuries), but it does make one wonder how he might expound in a more private setting. When asked about possible injuries to Dwight Phllips, Coach Smart answered “Fine. Probably more tired than hurt.” Similarly, about Ellis Robinson, the answer was “He looks good. Hopefully he’ll be good to go. We’ll find out more today.” That’s pretty positive, and pretty wordy from Kirby. And not a single mention of telling the media to wait until the availability report. Basketball is here, whether you recognize it’s existence before February or not. Head Men’s Coach Mike White comes into his 4th season in Athens, having already notched more wins in his first 3 campaigns than any previous Bulldog

item.title: "My Granddad Got Me a City Shirt" - Elliot Anderson Opens Up on Childhood Affection for Manchester City
item.description: "My Granddad Got Me a City Shirt" - Elliot Anderson Opens Up on Childhood Affection for Manchester City Elliot Anderson has donned sky blue beneath Newcastle's black and white since childhood. Not every summer arrival hits the ground running, which makes City fans especially quick to warm to those players that do manage to slot right in. Summer signing Elliot Anderson certainly fits into that category. So far, adapting to life under Enzo Maresca has been smooth sailing, earning the midfielder acclaim from fans and pundits - and now a nomination for the Etihad Player of the Month award for October. Beyond his obvious impact on the pitch, the 23-year-old has quickly connected with supporters through his humility and sincerity when handling media duties away from the grass. After spending more than a decade in Newcastle United’s youth and senior ranks, followed by an impressive two-year spell at Nottingham Forest, the possessionally dominant style of Manchester City was always going to represent a major shift. However, the midfielder has taken the step in his stride and cites the instant backing he received from City supporters as a key factor in his swift acclimatisation. In a recent interview for the November edition of Manchester City's official magazine , Anderson discussed his enduring connection with the club and how backing from the terraces helped him move past a challenging debut. "The Manchester City fans have been great to me from the first minute I played and really supported me and got behind me," Anderson said. Obviously, my first game was in the Community Shield and wasn't my best performance, but I think the fans really sort of stuck with me and hopefully I’ve started to repay them." That bond has translated into stellar form on the pitch, with exceptional performances at Old Trafford and Anfield among the highlights. With Manchester City competing fiercely across domestic and European fronts, the midfielder's combative and composed displays have given Enzo Maresca a must-start name in the engine room. A childhood affinity for the Blues While Anderson's footballing education took place in the North East during his long association with Newcastle, his ties to the Blues do stretch back further than his recent transfer. Growing up with a soft spot for Manchester City, the midfielder revealed how a gift from his grandad during his childhood left a lasting impression. "I think I joined Newcastle U9s and left when I was about 21," the England midfielder added. "I was a long time at the club, and I loved it. "Obviously, I've always been a Newcastle fan, all my family have, but everyone has a second club and that was City for me. "My grandad got me a City shirt, I think around the 2010-11 season, and I was about eight at the time. It was something I’d just wear around the house - outside I was always in a Newcastle top." Manchester City now prepare for a visit to RB Leipzig in midweek before Anderson returns to face his old club Nottingham F

item.title: “Worst Starting QB in the League”: NFL Fans Rip Sam Darnold Over Lack of Awareness After Throwing Costly Int in Seahawks’ Loss vs. Bears
item.description: Sam Darnold © Instagram (@/samdarnold) Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is taking a lot of flak for a costly mistake on Monday. In the fourth quarter against the Chicago Bears, the quarterback tried to throw a pass on a third-and-7 play. However, a Bears player tipped the ball before it landed in the hands of defensive lineman James Lynch. He then ran deep into the Seahawks’ territory. D’Andre Swift then scored a five-yard rushing TD to seal a 34-17 win for the Bears. Fans on social media did not shy away from criticizing Sam Darnold for his underwhelming performance. “Sam Darnold is the worst starting QB in the league,” one fan said. Against the Bears, Darnold completed 17-of-34 passes for 188 yards, two TDs and an INT. Meanwhile, Caleb Williams completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and a TD. Sam Darnold joined the Seattle Seahawks on a three-year, $100.5 million deal last year. During the 2025 season, he threw for 4,048 yards and 25 TDs in the regular season, leading his team to victory in Super Bowl LX. However, this season has been a roller coaster ride for the veteran. Before Monday’s loss to the Bears, he played in six games and threw for 1,290 yards and eight TDs, along with eight INTs. Darnold missed Week 2 against the Cardinals with a hip tendon strain. Emmanuel Acho shares his thoughts on the Bears beating Sam Darnold and the Seahawks The Chicago Bears headed to Lumen Field on Monday after back-to-back wins over the Atlanta Falcons and the New England Patriots. With this victory over the Super Bowl LX champions, they improve to 6-2. On the “Speakeasy” show, Emmanuel Acho praised Ben Johnson and his team for emerging victorious on the road against the Seahawks. “The Chicago Bears bullied the bullies,” Acho said. “You went into Seattle and you saw a team that just punked the Chiefs last week, and you punked them. You punched them in the face over and over. Jeffery Simmons, that’s quite a debut. Five tackles, two TFLs, a sack. “Now (with Simmons on the team), they do not have to blitz. Now you can get pressure by just rushing forward. … You have an extra defender to play coverage. As a result, the Seahawks offense could not even get going. 19 carries, only 81 yards. Sam Darnold was running for his life. Though there were only three sacks, dude got pressure on 10 or so snaps. At the end of the day, the Bears are probably the most dangerous team in the NFL.” The Bears will next face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Nov. 8. item.title: La Liga president Javier Tebas accuses Real Madrid of dragging out Negreira case to ruin Barcelona's reputation
item.description: GFX Javier Tebas Florentino Perez - Getty/GOAL La Liga president Javier Tebas has accused Real Madrid of intentionally prolonging the Negreira case to cause maximum reputational damage to Barcelona. The league chief suggests that the constant legal appeals from the capital are a strategic move to keep the scandal in the headlines. Tebas questions Madrid's motives Spanish courts are currently investigating payments made by Barcelona to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the Referees’ Technical Committee (CTA). While no evidence has proven sporting corruption, Los Blancos have aggressively targeted their Clasico rivals over the scandal . Tebas has now publicly condemned the capital club's approach. He claims their sudden interest in the investigation only began after Barcelona withdrew from the controversial European Super League project, accusing them of weaponising the legal system to hurt the Blaugrana. 'Stretching it like chewing gum' The league chief did not hold back when assessing Madrid's behaviour, suggesting paranoia has taken hold at the Bernabeu. "They are stretching the Negreira case like chewing gum. Real Madrid thinks Negreira is in every referee’s dressing room at every stadium where Real Madrid plays," Tebas stated during World In Progress (WIP) congress, as quoted by AS . "I remind Real Madrid that we went to the prosecutor’s office before Real Madrid did. The president of Real Madrid was on the board of directors for six months after the Negreira issue came to light. In a general assembly, he defended the club of his then-friend while it was in the Super League. The day Barca left, it seems everything changed." Unacceptable attacks on Barcelona Tebas believes the continued assault on Barcelona's public image is unwarranted while the judicial process is ongoing. "It must be clearly stated that what is happening with the constant attacks against Barcelona is unacceptable because this is a drawn-out affair," Tebas continued. "Barcelona will have to assume their responsibilities if necessary, but right now they cannot be blamed for anything because it is Real Madrid that is asking for the process to be prolonged." He concluded: "Barca’s case has nothing to do with Manchester City’s, and that cannot influence the justice system. The decision must be made here, in Spain." A Spanish resolution The Spanish judicial system will continue its investigation at its own pace, independently of other high-profile football cases across Europe. Tebas has explicitly distanced the Catalan club's situation from Manchester City's ongoing battle with the Premier League, insisting the verdict in England will not impact proceedings in Spain. Until a definitive legal conclusion is reached, the bitter off-pitch war of words between Spain's two biggest clubs shows no signs of slowing down.

item.title: Gunmen abduct two visually impaired persons in Plateau, demand N50m ransom
item.description: … as seven escape By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have abducted two visually impaired persons along Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State while they were returning to Jos from Benue State, with their abductors demanding N50 million ransom for their release. The victims were among nine persons travelling in a vehicle to attend a training programme in Benue State, while seven others reportedly escaped when the vehicle came under attack on Monday night. Chairman of the Plateau State chapter of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPWD), Shindol Aaron, who confirmed the incident, said the victims were abducted around 8pm in Riyom LGA. He said, “They were selected to attend a training in Benue State and, from what I gathered, they took off from Jos.” “Along the way, they got information that the event had been postponed to another day, and they were asked to return to their station.” “So, it was on their way back to Jos that they encountered some kidnappers who abducted them.” “They were nine in the vehicle. Seven of them escaped, and two were abducted. So, right now, we have a male and a lady in their custody.” According to him, the abductors had established contact with someone in connection with the release of the victims. He said, “This incident happened yesterday, Monday, in the night, around 8pm around Riyom LGA.” “I have not spoken with the kidnappers, but I was told that they were asking for ransom from somebody who spoke with them.” Aaron said the incident had been reported to security agencies, adding that efforts were ongoing to secure the release of the victims. He said, “We have reported the incident to the security agents, and we are trying to see how they could be released.” “The driver of the vehicle also went to the police station to report.” Another member of the association, Ishaya Ayuba Danjatau, who also confirmed the abduction, said the kidnappers had demanded an N50 million ransom. The member said, “The kidnappers have reached out, and they are demanding N50 million before they can free the two persons in their custody. “Where do they want us to get the money from?” Efforts to obtain the reaction of the Plateau State Police Command spokesman, DSP Alabo Alfred, were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen abduct two visually impaired persons in Plateau, demand N50m ransom appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘I stand by’… Bill Simmons doubles down on LA Lakers ownership group claims
item.description: Photo by Rebecca Sapp/Getty Images for The Recording Academy Podcaster Bill Simmons has doubled down on the claims he made about the Los Angeles Lakers . Earlier this year, Mark Walter made the surprise decision to sell the LA Lakers after little more than a year of ownership. A new ownership group led by Bob Iger and Josh Kushner bought Walter out, but the deal is yet to be finalized. Last week, Bill Simmons caused a stir by claiming that the new group do not yet have the money to complete the buyout. ESPN has since reported that all terms of the deal have been agreed – but Simmons is sticking by his claims. Speaking on his most recent podcast, Simmons said: “They put out all these different pieces about they do have the money, but they didn’t actually say they had the money. “I see both sides. I think they’re confident they are gonna get the money. But I’ve talked to too many people who said they’re still looking to find the remaining money to pay $12.5 billion.” He added: “I think they probably will get the money, but I don’t think they have it yet because too many people have been shown the deck and offered it and offered a chance to get in.” Lakers sale is new record price The $12.5 billion agreement for the LA Lakers is a new record for a sports franchise, in excess of the $10 billion Walter paid in 2025. Simmons added: “It seems a little high. I’d kind of wanna own my own arena for $12.5bn. Anyway, I stand by what I said.” ESPN’s report said that Walter and Kushner have not yet signed a formal agreement, despite having a total agreement. item.title: Biggest trick Celtic have ever missed, not getting Jens Berthel Askou
item.description: Biggest trick Celtic have ever missed, not getting Jens Berthel Askou Charlie Mulgrew and Kevin Thomson have been discussing Martin O’Neill’s time at Celtic after a run of only three wins in ten matches has left the legendary manager facing calls from some supporters for him to stand aside… 1st November 2026; Falkirk Stadium, Scottish Premiership, Falkirk versus Celtic; Celtic manager Martin O’Neill. Photo Vagelis Georgariou And Thomson, speaking on The Breakdown podcast , made a very interesting point on what he regards as a huge opportunity Celtic missed out on during the summer when they passed on the chance to bring former Motherwell manager Jens Berthel Askou into the club to replace Martin O’Neill. Mulgrew pointed out that Martin O’Neill was just a stopgap and would give the club time to sort out all the issues in the background, including sourcing a Head of Recruitment, improving the stadium and so on. Martin O’Neill celebrating title victory. Thomson explained his point: “I do think, and it’s easy viewpoint on how it looked last year, I did think how dramatic the last day of the season was, he should’ve just up sticks and left. But I still felt the club would be missing a trick. “I think Martin would’ve been a brilliant foil, mentor or sounding board, somebody to speak to, somebody to confide in as part of whatever that looked like for Celtic, for the new manager coming in. “Now he’s been the manager; he’s had it for a longer period of time rather than just short-term, you kind of feel as though Martin O’Neill wouldn’t work because he’s now attached himself to being the manager.” Motherwell manager Jens Berthel Askou is seen during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Motherwell at Celtic Park on March 14, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Charlie Mulgrew added his own thoughts saying: “If he walks away then, Celtic still weighed him in with good money because he deserved that because of what he did with the title and then gave it to a Jens Berthel Askou and let Martin O’Neill be director of football or be on the board or whatever.” Thomson agreed and was emphatic in his assessment on Celtic passing over Askou and instead offering the job to Martin O’Neill for one year with a second year option. “ It’s the biggest trick Celtic have ever missed, not getting him,” he said. Mulgrew picked up on that, pointing out that : “It’s a big one, isn’t it? I think he would have been desperate for it. He was always at Celtic Park.” Ange Postecoglou, Manager of Celtic, embraces Liel Abada after winning the Scottish Premiership following the match between Hearts and Celtic at Tynecastle Park on May 07, 2023. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Thomson noted: “You think of the resources that he would’ve had at his disposal and the type of players. item.title: El Nino Watch: The impacts around the world this week
item.description: With torrential rains in India and Nepal, and drought already devastating South America, this year’s exceptionally strong El Nino is being felt across the globe. It threatens rice and coffee harvests to such an extent that the World Bank expects food prices to rise by 18 percent next year. Here is how El Nino is playing out across AFP’s network. – Cyclone lashes India – Ferocious winds and torrential rain lashed India’s southeastern coast after a cyclone made landfall on Wednesday, killing at least three people and triggering nearly 100,000 evacuations. “Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water,” said Rajeshwari, 65, who gave only one name, after being taken to a government-run shelter near Kakinada, close to the heart of the storm. Cyclones, called hurricanes in the North Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific, are a regular menace in the Bay of Bengal and northern Indian Ocean. The storm season, however, has been turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has contributed to unprecedented warming. Cyclone Arnab then moved on towards Nepal, bringing heavy snowfall to the high Himalayan regions and intense rain through Saturday. – Bolivia declares state of emergency – In Bolivia, drought is affecting 78,000 families in six of the country’s nine departments and has led to the loss of more than 75,000 cattle, according to a government report this week. On Saturday, the Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz declared a state of emergency to free up resources for dealing with the impact of El Nino. “This will be a phenomenon that will have very severe impacts in terms of drought and floods, and we need the cooperation of all institutions,” Paz said. In neighbouring countries such as Peru, El Nino has ramped up temperatures and triggered forest fires that have already claimed the lives of at least 12 people. It has also helped spread the tropical disease dengue fever. In Chile meanwhile it is behind the rainiest October ever recorded in Santiago. – El Nino in numbers – According to the World Bank, food prices are expected to rise by 18 percent between 2025 and 2027, a surge explained both by supply difficulties caused by conflicts and by the anticipated effects of El Nino. Since June, the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab estimates that 484,500 excess heat-related deaths have occurred globally due to the weather phenomenon. The organisation projects about 373,000 additional deaths could occur over the next six months. – Vulnerable crops – Coffee, cocoa, rice… in this “Super” El Nino year, what are the most vulnerable crops? The answer depends on the region, but “from a food-security perspective, the crops of greatest concern are staple foods because they provide the bulk of calories consumed by populations in vulnerable countries,” Maximo Torero, chief economist at the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), told AFP. item.title: UK.gov lacks understanding of climate impact, says watchdog
item.description: Public bodies in the UK expect higher operating costs and energy charges as a result of climate changes and the transition to lower carbon energy, but few have a good picture of the risks, according to government auditors. A new report from the National Audit Office (NAO) says some public bodies expect financial impact from the risks they identified, although bodies were often not able to cost these – even approximately. "Bodies anticipate costs to arise from damage to assets and infrastructure, driven by physical damage from extreme weather, as well as from chronic shifts to higher temperatures and more precipitation. Bodies also expect higher maintenance and repair costs, potential asset upgrades, and transition costs. Many bodies expect increased operating costs, including energy charges. Bodies controlling significant property or infrastructure are particularly concerned with decarbonization and adaptation costs," the report stated. His Majesty’s Treasury (HMT) has set out rules for climate-related financial disclosure in larger central government bodies' annual reports, which produced their first set of reports for the 2025-26 financial year. Other rules for disclosure have been in place since 2022. However, the NAO found [PDF] that understanding of the risks in the impact of climate change – increasing temperatures, higher risk of flooding, higher winds and longer droughts – was poor, as was insight into costs of moving to a low-carbon economy. "Bodies did not articulate transition risks as well as physical risks in the strategy disclosures. In the disclosures we reviewed, while several transition risks were listed, few specifics were given, unlike physical risks, which were explained in greater detail," the report from the watchdog stated. "The transition risks most frequently identified included the financial cost of transition, and supply chain disruption. Anticipated transition costs included the costs of: switching to lower-carbon energy sources, including investments in new technology; complying with new regulations; and of fluctuations in the price and availability of materials, water, energy and specialist skills," it added. Gareth Davies, head of the NAO, said: "UK public services will need to adapt to the impacts of climate change. Parliament needs clear information on the resilience of infrastructure, service provision and finances to climate change, and on how these risks are being managed." "Although public bodies are still learning how best to report their most pressing climate risks, the requirement on all large central government bodies to make such disclosures from 2025-26 is an important first step. We expect this reporting to become more useful over time." Earlier this year a report from Global Action Plan, a climate charity, claimed 84 percent of proposed datacenter developments were in areas that are already water stressed or projected to be water stressed by 2040. item.title: Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel dies after collision during match
item.description: Spanish football club CD Tenerife have confirmed the death of their striker, Jesús de Miguel, aged 30, following a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a Spanish second division match. The footballer died on Tuesday, November 3, a day after the incident occurred during Tenerife’s league encounter with Andorra at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium. The collision happened towards the closing stages of the match, when De Miguel went for a loose ball and Owono rushed out of his goal to clear it. The goalkeeper, who was outside his penalty area, collided heavily with the striker, leaving him unconscious on the pitch. Medical personnel immediately rushed to attend to De Miguel, who was treated for several minutes before being carried off on a stretcher and taken to the University Hospital of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria. The match, which was tied at 2-2, was eventually abandoned in the 108th minute to allow medical personnel to attend to the injured player. Owono was shown a red card following the challenge. Reports from Spanish media indicated that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest following the collision but was resuscitated by medical personnel in the ambulance. Although his condition initially appeared stable, it deteriorated in the early hours of Tuesday. Confirming his death, CD Tenerife announced that the striker passed away at 8am on Tuesday. In a statement expressing its grief, the club said: “Broken with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.” The club added: “There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can ease this feeling of overwhelming sadness. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones and the entire Tenerife family, who mourn this cruel outcome.” It also conveyed its condolences to his family, friends, teammates and supporters. De Miguel’s family thanked those who had sent messages of support and appealed for privacy during the difficult period. The incident has attracted tributes from football clubs and supporters across Spain, with Barcelona and Real Madrid among those expressing condolences. item.title: Iran Unveils Billboard With Threat Against Trump’s Life
item.description: Iran unveiled a massive billboard and banners pledging to kill US President Donald Trump across Tehran on Tuesday, bringing to a new level the official rhetoric displayed in the capital. “We will kill Trump”, read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Tehran, which depicted the US president behind bars with his head bowed. New designs of billboards and displays mocking and vowing revenge against Trump have frequently been set up around Tehran since the war began on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic Republic’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iranians wave flags during a gathering in front of an anti-US billboard depicting US President Donald Trump in Tehran’s Enghelab Square on November 3, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP In recent days, renewed diplomatic efforts have been underway to bring Tehran and Washington to the table to prevent a resumption of fighting that has spread across the region and driven prices up globally. Trump, who on Tuesday faces crucial US midterm elections amid voter discontent driven in part by the Iran war, has said that a deal “could happen”. A visitor walks past a painting at an art exhibition against US President Donald Trump, in Tajrish Square in Tehran on November 2, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP In the busy Tajrish Square in northern Tehran, an open-air exhibition featured paintings of Trump, including one showing him with his face lying bloodied on the ground as a foot presses down on his head. Another depicted a bomb obscuring his face, in an apparent reference to Belgian surrealist René Magritte’s 1964 painting “The Son of Man”. Visitors walk past a painting at an art exhibition against US President Donald Trump, in Tajrish Square in Tehran on November 2, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP Nearby, a life-sized replica of a jail cell has remained on display, with an actor impersonating Trump spending the day inside. An adjacent screen showed images of the damage caused by US strikes on Iran. Tehran accuses Trump of deliberately targeting civilian sites during the war, including a school and a wedding ceremony, killing dozens of people including women and children. State-sponsored billboards and murals have been a fixture of Iran’s public spaces since the 1979 Islamic revolution, used to honour allies, celebrate military figures and send political messages to adversaries, particularly the United States and Israel. AFP The post Iran Unveils Billboard With Threat Against Trump’s Life appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Kebbi Govt Accuses ADC Of Politicising Private Land Dispute
item.description: The Kebbi State Government has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of politicising a private land dispute in Birnin Kebbi, alleging that the opposition party is spreading misinformation for political gains. The government said investigations by the Ministry of Lands and Housing established that the disputed property, located along Sani Abacha Bypass in Birnin Kebbi, belongs to a private businessman, Alhaji Umar Muhammad Gulumbe. It also accused the opposition party of misrepresenting previous security incidents in the state. Addressing a press conference, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed, said the controversy followed the demolition of a building on the disputed property on November 26. He explained that the incident attracted public attention after videos circulated on social media, alleging that the state government had deployed earth-moving equipment to demolish a property belonging to the ADC. The Commissioner, however, dismissed the allegations, insisting that the incident was a private land dispute between individuals and had no involvement of the state government. According to him, Umar Muhammad Gulumbe presented documents to establish ownership of the property, including a Certificate of Occupancy reportedly signed by former Governor Senator Adamu Aliero. Ahmed further disclosed that Gulumbe had reported the alleged trespass to the police and submitted a petition to the Ministry of Lands and Housing, which subsequently investigated the matter. He maintained that the state government had no prior involvement in the demolition, stressing that any disagreement over ownership should be resolved through the appropriate legal channels. The Commissioner challenged anyone laying claim to the property to present relevant ownership documents before a competent court rather than resorting to social media allegations. He also called on political actors to exercise restraint in their public statements, warning that the spread of unverified information could heighten political tension and threaten peaceful coexistence in the state. However, the full circumstances surrounding the disputed property, including the competing claims and allegations, remain subject to independent verification and, where necessary, determination by the appropriate authorities. The post Kebbi Govt Accuses ADC Of Politicising Private Land Dispute appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Gambia Central Bank’s planned sack affects 57 Nigerians, NiDCOM kicks
item.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom The Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NIDCOM) has kicked against a directive by the Central Bank of The Gambia ordering banks to sack non-Gambian employees. Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NIDCOM, Mrs Abike Dabiri-Erewa, described the September 16 directive as deeply worrisome, saying it threatens the jobs of 57 Nigerian professionals. Dabiri-Erewa, in a statement by NIDCOM spokesman Abdur-Rahman Balogun, said the Central Bank of The Gambia (CBG) had given banks till December 31, 2026, to replace all non-Gambian staff with Gambians. NIDCOM said the affected Nigerians work with four Nigerian-owned banks and hold valid residency and work permits. The Commission noted that the four banks are major players in the Gambian economy, controlling 37.2 per cent of total deposits valued at GMD35.3 billion, 32.6 per cent of loans amounting to GMD7.67 billion and 37 per cent of industry assets worth GMD44.78 billion. The banks, it added, also account for 34.5 per cent of investments in Central Bank bonds and provided 90 per cent of funding for the National Water and Electricity Company, NAWEC. While acknowledging The Gambia’s right to promote local employment, Dabiri-Erewa said such policy must respect existing contracts, valid work permits and ECOWAS protocols on free movement. She said, “It is contradictory to encourage African investment and regional cooperation while displacing qualified African professionals.” NIDCOM urged the apex bank to reverse the blanket directive and engage the Nigerian High Commission in Banjul and other stakeholders for an amicable resolution. It also called on Gambian authorities to uphold the spirit of ECOWAS integration and the long-standing cordial relations between Nigeria and The Gambia. The post Gambia Central Bank’s planned sack affects 57 Nigerians, NiDCOM kicks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Oxfam's Destroy and Rebuild Index: 'Wealthy minority of investors benefit from both sides of crisis'
item.description: The world's most vulnerable populations bear the brunt and the costs of the climate crisis, while the wealthy and powerful profit. Oxfam France’s Climate Inequality Advocacy Officer Selma Huart examines the relationship between concentrated wealth, unequal exposure to disasters and investors profiting from both polluting industries and reconstruction. “They are burning the planet, benefiting from it, but they are also benefiting from rebuilding,” she explains. Huart places redistribution at the centre of climate policy, calling for taxes on wealthy polluters to finance protection for vulnerable communities.

item.title: Kano APC dismisses Kwankwaso’s allegation over missing NDC guber candidate’s name
item.description: The APC in Kano has dismissed Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso’s claim that it and Gov. Abba Yusuf omitted NDC candidate’s name from INEC list. The candidate in question is Aminu Abdussalam-Gwarzo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). This is contained in a statement issued by the Chairman, All Progressives Congress (APC), Kano State, Alhaji Umar Haruna-Doguwa, made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Kano. “The party described the allegation as false, baseless and an attempt by Kwankwaso to blackmail the APC and its governorship candidate. “The APC maintained that the case originated from the internal crisis within the NDC. “Neither the party nor Gov. Yusuf has any involvement whatsoever in the legal proceedings surrounding the NDC candidate. “It was instituted by party members against the NDC itself, and not by the APC, its governorship candidate or the Kano State Government,” he said. The chairman stressed that attempts to associate the APC and its candidate with the matter were misleading and intended to shift attention from the internal challenges confronting the NDC. Haruna-Doguwa said the party distanced itself from the legal proceedings, insisting that neither the APC nor its governorship candidate sponsored, influenced or facilitated the court action against Abdussalam-Gwarzo. “The judiciary is an independent arm of government and neither the APC nor its governorship candidate has the authority to dictate its proceedings or decisions,” he said. He challenged Sen. Kwankwaso to provide credible and verifiable evidence linking the APC or Gov. Yusuf to the case, rather than making allegations capable of misleading the public and creating unnecessary political tension. “The APC described the allegation as an unfortunate attempt at political blackmail, particularly coming from Sen. Kwankwaso, who is the Vice-Presidential candidate of the NDC,” he said. Haruna-Doguwa added that every eligible candidate has the constitutional right to participate in the 2027 general elections in accordance with the law. He reaffirmed the APC’s commitment to democratic principles and welcomed the participation of opposition parties in the electoral process, stressing that it has no reason to plot against any political party or candidate. The chairman called on the public to disregard attempts to associate the APC and its governorship candidate with the NDC’s internal legal battle. Haruna-Doguwa reiterated that neither the party nor its candidate had any hand, directly or indirectly, in the proceedings or any decision concerning the party’s candidate. (NAN) The post Kano APC dismisses Kwankwaso’s allegation over missing NDC guber candidate’s name appeared first on Vanguard News .

The incident reportedly occurred after a disagreement between the deceased and the motorcyclist over payment of an agreed fare, triggering tension in the area and disrupting commercial activities. An eyewitness said the disagreement began after Kehinde allegedly failed to honour an agreement reached with the rider over the fare, leading to a heated argument that escalated into a physical confrontation. It was gathered that during the altercation, the motorcyclist allegedly brought out a sharp object and stabbed the boxer. Kehinde reportedly sustained fatal injuries and died following the attack. The killing has heightened tension around Olodo Garage, with commercial motorcyclists reportedly withdrawing their services amid fears of possible reprisal attacks. The withdrawal has disrupted transportation in the area, forcing commuters to trek long distances to their destinations, while traders and other residents have also been affected by the disruption to daily activities. Confirming the incident in a telephone conversation with our correspondent, the Oyo State Police Public Relations Officer, Ayanlade Olayinka, said the matter was under investigation. item.title: North Korea test fires strategic cruise missiles
item.description: North Korea test-fired strategic cruise missiles, state media reported Tuesday, in the latest display of its weapons capabilities as tensions persist on the Korean peninsula. The Monday launch came a day after North Korea tested cluster bomb warheads, as tensions with Seoul have risen after a landmine blast along their heavily fortified border wounded three South Korean soldiers. “The middle-sized dispersal warhead tipped on the cruise missile is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 5 to 6 hectares with its highest-density power,” the official Korean Central News Agency reported Tuesday. The test “perfected the capability to deliver a vertical strike against the target by improving the terminal maneuverability of the cruise missile,” KCNA said, “taking into consideration the natural and geographical characteristics of the targeted area.” A North Korean official was quoted as saying the test was conducted “because our armed forces should defend the security of the country and deter all sorts of threats.” “Various combat functions of such strongest weapon system will help defend the DPRK from potential threats from outside and renew the military capabilities of the state,” the general director of the Missile Administration said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. The nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile. South Korea’s military did not announce the cruise missile launch, as it had also not done with Sunday’s test. Unlike ballistic missile launches, North Korean cruise missile tests are not prohibited by UN Security Council sanctions. Asked Monday about Sunday’s reported test, Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Jang Do-young said South Korea and the United States were “closely coordinating and conducting a highly detailed analysis of its characteristics and specifications”. “Our military does not announce all projectiles launched by North Korea,” said Jang. “Whether to make an announcement is determined through a comprehensive military assessment, taking into account the protection of surveillance and reconnaissance assets and capabilities, operational security and other factors,” he added. The post North Korea test fires strategic cruise missiles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Raspberry Pi hikes prices again, barely a month after the last round
item.description: Raspberry Pi has announced yet another round of price hikes, this time adding $80 to the cost of its 16GB Pi 5, which now sells for more than three times its original launch price. The latest bump, announced by Raspberry Pi boss Eben Upton, takes the 16GB Pi 5 to a whopping $385. The 16GB Compute Module 5 variants are also getting $40 more expensive, although the Raspberry Pi 500+, which packs the same amount of RAM, has escaped this particular round. Upton blamed a familiar culprit: soaring memory costs, worsened by a lack of alternative suppliers for 16GB DRAM and ongoing shortages of other components. "Unfortunately, a lack of alternative supply for 16GB DRAM, compounded by other ongoing component shortages, means we now need to make further price increases on some of our highest-density products," Upton wrote. It's becoming an expensive habit for Raspberry Pi customers. The 16GB Pi 5 cost $120 when it launched in January 2025, which seems almost reasonable now. Raspberry Pi added $25 in December, another $60 in February, and a further $100 in April . With today's $80 increase, buyers are being asked to cough up $265 more than they were less than two years ago, a price hike of 221 percent. And it's barely been a month since Raspberry Pi raised prices on its 2GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 models by $12.50 apiece, taking them to $67.50 and $77.50 respectively. The repeated markups come despite Raspberry Pi reporting record first-half results in September. Revenue jumped 90 percent to $256.9 million, while gross profit rose 79 percent to $59.4 million. Gross profit per board climbed 53 percent to $12.20, helped partly by memory purchased before prices went through the roof. That stockpile advantage has since largely disappeared. For customers unwilling to pay nearly $400 for a single-board computer, Upton advises buying something with less RAM, using an older Pi, or optimizing applications to make do with less memory. He also warned that some sellers are exploiting the shortages by charging inflated prices or offering products that aren't what they appear to be, urging customers to stick to approved resellers. “We’re aware that a few bad actors have been taking advantage of the current memory supply circumstances to sell Raspberry Pi products at inflated prices or shift products that aren’t what they seem,” he said. There is, apparently, some good news, as Raspberry Pi continues to insist the increases are temporary. "As we've said from the beginning, the current memory landscape is difficult but ultimately temporary, and we look forward to rolling back our price increases when memory costs fall once again," Upton wrote. That could be a long wait. Micron has previously warned that memory shortages could drag on into 2028 or beyond, so anyone hoping to see a $120 Pi 5 again probably shouldn't hold their breath. ®

item.title: Everyone has the file. Nobody has the right version
item.description: Distributed teams need to collaborate on shared information, but duplicated files, delays, and competing versions keep getting in the way. Picture a video production team with editors in different cities. One person updates a project file, another keeps working from an earlier copy, and a third waits for a large transfer to finish. When teams need to collaborate on large files across locations, traditional storage and file-sharing arrangements introduce friction precisely where people expect technology to help. Collaboration shouldn't require detective work The hard part isn't merely moving a file. It's knowing who has the authoritative copy, when changes are available, and whether somebody else is still working on an outdated version. Consider a game studio preparing a build for review. A designer exports an updated asset, but a colleague pulls an older version from a synced folder. The mistake only becomes obvious when the pieces are assembled. The team must trace the mismatch, resend files, and repeat work. Sync-and-download workflows depend on a chain of uploads, downloads, and decisions about which copy is current. Under deadline pressure, that chain breaks. Delayed access means missed handoffs; duplicated files mean extra checking and sometimes rework. For IT, each workaround creates another question: where does the data live, who can access it, and how do teams maintain consistent controls? Adding another collaboration application doesn't resolve those underlying questions. The useful starting point is the workflow. Find out where teams copy data, where they wait, and what prompts them to work outside the shared system. Compare notes with peers These frustrations cut across industries, but the ways organizations respond aren't identical. Hearing how another team handled version confusion, access, and handoffs is often more useful than another abstract promise of seamless collaboration. That's the focus of The Register and LucidLink’s invitation-only dinner on November 24 at Covent Garden Hotel in London. Joe Fay of The Register will moderate a peer discussion under the Chatham House Rule. Bring the real situations that never fit neatly into a technology diagram, and hear how others are handling them. item.title: Legendary Musician Youssou N’Dour Lights Up the Stage at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 | Watch Highlights
item.description: African music legend, Youssou N’Dour, performing live at the Goalkeepers Dakar 2026. Photo by Seye Kehinde. On the 29th of October, 2026, Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 brought together global leaders, changemakers and young people to discuss how AI can help build a more equitable future. While the conversations explored the opportunities and challenges of using technology to advance progress, the event also made room for music and celebration. One of its special moments was a live performance by Senegalese music legend Youssou N’Dour , whose performance brought the audience to their feet. Youssou N’Dour is a Senegalese singer and politician who helped develop a style of popular Senegambian music known as mbalax that blends Wolof traditional instrumental and vocal forms primarily with Cuban and other Latin American popular genres. item.title: Forget retraining - AI can now tweak another AI's weights
item.description: The outputs of AI models are the result of a complex interplay between neurons, weights, training, and inference, and are therefore difficult to follow. But in some ways they're starting to look more like open books. Recent work by Anthropic safety fellow Joshua Fonseca Rivera has revealed how certain neurons in a neural network can be associated with a specific persona . Now, computer scientists from MIT's Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) have found that frontier AI models like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can rewrite the weights of another model directly, as opposed to indirectly through training, and alter their behavior. "We find early signs that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading, writing, and reasoning about neural network weights," said Rikiya Takehi, a PhD student at MIT CSAIL, in a social media post . "Instead of training, models may treat raw weights like readable, editable code: diagnosing failures and patching them directly." To demonstrate that, Takehi and colleagues Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to make it better at math. Astra changed only 0.016 percent of the model's weights, reducing its reasoning loops and improving its math performance by as much as sixfold on the MATH-500 benchmark, while boosting its instruction-following score on the IFEval benchmark roughly threefold. There was no training using gradient descent ; Astra just revised the numerical values that constitute Qwen's weights. "All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops," the researchers wrote in a blog post . "It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming. "Throughout the history of deep learning, we encoded our simplistic inductive biases into tiny symbolic optimizers like Adam or Muon. This is changing: our neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about their weights." Astra's ability to program weights extends to being able to write a neural network from scratch, zero-shot. The researchers told Astra: "write, from scratch, the weights of a policy network that plays [Breakout] as well as possible." And it did so. Takehi suggests this technique shows promise for improving models without the consequences of catastrophic forgetting , which can occur when a model is revised to include new knowledge. More generally, the authors expect Weight-Space Programming will open the door to new ways to understand models and optimize them, and to implement recursive self-improvement. The technique may also prove useful for reducing model sycophancy and improving interpretability and alignment. The next step, the authors say, involves building a benchmark and a harness for carrying out Weight-Space Programming on LLMs. "We believe this will provide a standardized evaluation to m

item.title: Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship
item.description: Political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration over what he described as extravagant lifestyles among public officials amid economic hardship in the country. Utomi said it was contradictory for government officials to describe Nigeria as poor while allegedly displaying luxury vehicles, including Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, and travelling in private jets. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Tuesday, arguing that the lifestyles of public office holders should reflect the economic realities confronting ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot stand before the world and declare that Nigeria is poor, then turn around and parade your ministers in million-dollar Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, while public officials fly around in private jets. Your optics contradict your narrative, your lifestyle contradicts your statistics,” he said. The former presidential candidate said if Nigeria was indeed poor, government spending and the management of public resources should reflect the country’s economic circumstances. He argued that members of the executive and legislature should demonstrate fiscal restraint, particularly when citizens were being asked to endure economic difficulties. According to him, public office should not be treated as a licence for extravagance, adding that government officials had a responsibility to show restraint in the use of public resources. “The APC needs to understand that public office is not a licence for extravagance. If citizens must endure economic hardship, those entrusted with their taxes must also demonstrate restraint,” Utomi said. He added that displaying luxury lifestyles while asking Nigerians to endure economic hardship could deepen public resentment and reinforce perceptions that government officials were insensitive to the plight of ordinary citizens. The post Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police rescue 11 kidnapped victims, arrest 19 suspects
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has rescued 11 kidnapped victims, arrested 19 suspects and recovered 91 rustled livestock, including 48 cows and 43 sheep, in security operations conducted across several states in the last 48 hours. The operations also led to the recovery of firearms, stolen valuables and motorcycles, while several attempted bandit attacks were foiled. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the operational breakthroughs in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operations were part of sustained efforts to combat kidnapping, terrorism, armed robbery, cultism, cattle rustling and other criminal activities. He said investigations and follow-up operations were ongoing to apprehend fleeing suspects, rescue more victims and recover stolen property. In Zamfara State, police tactical operatives, working with local vigilantes, rescued five elderly women abducted by armed bandits while harvesting beans in Dansadau, Maru Local Government Area. The victims were freed following a gun battle that forced the abductors to flee. However, a 35-year-old farmer was killed during the attack. In Niger State, a joint security team comprising police, military personnel, Department of State Services operatives, special hunters and vigilantes rescued six farmers abducted at Mahangi village, near Pandogari in Rafi Local Government Area. The victims were subsequently taken to a police division for documentation and reunion with their families. In Kebbi State, joint security forces repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa terrorists on Ribah town in Danko Wasagu Local Government Area on October 30, after the attackers attempted to block Rambo Junction. The operation followed an earlier attack on Dan-Indo village in Fakai Local Government Area, where nine people were killed, while two vehicles and several motorcycles were set ablaze. The police said security operatives had been deployed to maintain order and sustain operations against the suspected terrorists. Also in Zamfara, police and soldiers have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation following the abduction of nine persons at Upa, near Kurya Madaro in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Bush-combing operations are ongoing in surrounding forests to secure their release and apprehend the perpetrators. In Kano State, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad arrested five suspects accused of harbouring criminals in connection with the abduction of the APC Chairman of Rogo Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdu Fanka. Although the principal suspects reportedly escaped, the police recovered 48 cows, 43 sheep and two Bajaj Boxer motorcycles from the location. In Katsina State, tactical teams foiled an attempted bandit attack on Karofi village in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area after responding to a distress call. The gunmen reportedly retreated into the bush following an exchange of gunfire. No casualty was recorded. In Lagos State, police arrested a 28-year-old suspected

item.title: 2027: Atiku’s presidency won’t determine Senate President, Reps Speaker — Melaye
item.description: The Deputy Director-General of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dino Melaye, has said a government led by Atiku Abubakar will not determine who becomes Senate President or Speaker of the House of Representatives. Melaye said the ADC would allow lawmakers to elect their leaders independently, insisting that the party was committed to democratic principles and an independent National Assembly. He stated this while answering questions on the oversight mechanisms the ADC would introduce to track government payments, fund releases and beneficiaries during an appearance on Arise Television’s Prime Time on Monday. “To start with, an Atiku presidency will not determine who is going to be the Senate president, the president of the Senate, or the Speaker of the House of Representatives,” he said. “Atiku is a Democrat. ADC is a very democratic political party. So we are going to allow the people to elect their leaders.” Melaye argued that allowing lawmakers to choose their leaders would promote legislative independence and strengthen the National Assembly’s oversight of the executive arm of government. “And I told you that wherever you have the members electing their leaders, there is some modicum of independence,” he said. “So to start with, the ADC will make sure that the National Assembly is truly independent, and if the National Assembly is truly independent, that will drive their oversight functions over the Executive.” On the mechanisms for scrutinising government spending, the ADC campaign official said relevant National Assembly committees would be empowered to question government officials and monitor expenditure. He specifically identified the Committees on Establishment, Finance, and Budget and Planning as possible channels for investigating government spending and ensuring accountability. “The Committee on Establishment is responsible for questioning this type of spenders because they have direct oversight function over the State House. The committee on finance is there. The committee on budget and planning is there,” Melaye said. “So you can use any of these committees at least to ask questions.” The post 2027: Atiku’s presidency won’t determine Senate President, Reps Speaker — Melaye appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Atiku faults Cross River security over alleged estate robberies
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has criticised the security arrangements around Cross River State Governor’s private residence in Calabar, following reports of alleged robberies in neighbouring homes. Atiku said residents of the estate where Governor Bassey Otu’s private residence is located had complained of repeated burglaries despite the presence of armed policemen and two roadblocks securing the governor’s property. According to him, one resident reportedly lost an air conditioner and a freezer to burglars, while another disclosed that two houses on a nearby street were attacked last week. The former Vice President disclosed this in a post on his X account on Tuesday, questioning the disparity between the security provided for the governor and the protection available to residents living in the same neighbourhood. He said the governor had been operating from his private residence for nearly three years while the Government House was undergoing renovation, yet residents living nearby remained exposed to security threats. “This is security, APC style: two roadblocks for the governor, and none for the people next door,” Atiku said. He questioned the capacity of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to address insecurity across the state, asking what it could offer communities outside the state capital if residents living beside the governor could not sleep without fear. Atiku also outlined his proposed security reforms, pledging to transform the Nigeria Police Force from what he described as a regime-protecting force into a citizen-focused public service. He said his administration would expand police personnel towards the international benchmark of one officer to every 450 citizens to improve security coverage across communities. The ADC presidential candidate also promised to establish community-based security and intelligence networks to enable neighbourhoods to identify and report threats before criminal activities occur. “Security that stops at the governor’s gate is not security; it is a fence,” he added. The post Atiku faults Cross River security over alleged estate robberies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How the New Tax Stamp Could Show Up in Everyday Life
item.description: We’ve all been there: planning a weekend dinner with friends, throwing a birthday bash, or just kicking back at home with a few favourite treats. Drinks and refreshments are basically a staple of these moments. But have you ever stopped to think about how behind-the-scenes government policies end up changing the price tags on those items? With the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) rolling out its new excise stamp policy in January 2026, that question is at the forefront, especially for brands that make things like alcohol, tobacco, and sugar-sweetened beverages. Honestly, nobody’s really stressing over the policy itself. What people care about is the ripple effect: how companies handle the new regulation and whether those adjustments will make our favourite items more expensive on the shelf. When Business Meets Your Wallet Behind every product is a mountain of decisions from packaging and distribution to compliance and production. Most of the time, we never see this happening, but it plays a huge role in how items are priced. When new regulations bring extra costs, companies find themselves at a crossroads. Some choose to absorb the blow internally to keep customers happy, while others might tweak their prices. It really comes down to the specific brand, the market, and how heavy the financial lift is. For everyday shoppers, that’s usually the moment a boring policy talk suddenly feels very real. What Does This Mean for How We Spend ? The change probably won’t hit overnight, and it might not even be dramatic. But over time, small shifts in everyday prices can change how we shop. You might find yourself comparing brands a bit more closely, hunting for promos and discounts, or rethinking how much cash you drop on certain treats. Brands, meanwhile, are caught in a tricky balancing act: keeping loyal customers without going broke on rising operating costs. Just keep in mind: a new tax stamp doesn’t automatically mean prices are shooting up. It all depends on how companies adapt and whether those extra costs trickle down to us. The Bigger Picture At the end of the day, this is really about finding a middle ground. The government wants solid systems to collect taxes, while businesses need a framework that lets them stay afloat and grow. But come to think of it, the authorities are already equipped with internal tracking solutions, such as electronic invoicing from FIRS alongside the Customs Service’s B’Odogwu digital excise register, rendering physical paper tags largely redundant. Striking that balance matters because business decisions don’t just stay on a spreadsheet. They shape the things we buy, the choices we make, and how we manage our money. Right now, it’s still a bit early to tell what the full impact on consumers will be. But staying clued in on what’s driving the market makes it a whole lot easier to navigate the changes coming our way. item.title: WARRI DELINEATION: Lawyer seeks probe, warns against political manipulation, violence
item.description: Lawyer and politician, Chief Robinson Ariyo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to investigate the Warri delineation exercise, saying there are allegations of financial inducement to favour some areas over others. Ariyo also called on the President to direct the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to provide an independent written legal opinion on the legality of the exercise. In a statement, he urged the President to direct relevant agencies to preserve all documents and records relating to the exercise and investigate allegations of financial misconduct, security compromises and electoral irregularities. He further called for an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly those whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records might be connected to the allegations surrounding the Warri delineation controversy. Ariyo also urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, and Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU, to investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel and security operatives in connection with the controversy. The statement reads: “That the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice be requested to provide an independent, written legal opinion on the legality of the ongoing Warri delineation exercise, identifying the applicable constitutional provisions, statutory powers, judicial orders and procedural requirements governing the exercise. The opinion should specifically distinguish between the delineation of electoral wards, State Constituencies and Federal Constituencies. “That INEC be formally requested, in the exercise of its constitutional independence, to publish the complete delineation report, supporting maps, methodology, relevant population and geographical data, stakeholder submissions and reasons for accepting or rejecting material objections. That the Commission be urged to undertake a transparent review of any substantiated procedural or factual irregularities and refrain from implementing any aspect found to be unlawful, subject always to applicable judicial orders and statutory requirements. “That all relevant documents, correspondence, meeting records, maps, electronic records, financial documents and administrative communications relating to the exercise be preserved against destruction, alteration or concealment. “That the appropriate federal authorities undertake an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly contracts whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records may be relevant to the allegations raised herein. As Otti govt secures int’l recognition for health reforms By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State has emerged as the preferred location for a proposed stroke and neurovascular centre to serve Nigeria and West Africa, following its participation in the 2026 Sweden-Africa Neurosurgery Symposium in Gothenburg, Sweden. The state Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this while briefing newsmen on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia. Kanu said the selection was in recognition of Abia’s strides in healthcare delivery and the availability of qualified medical specialists, describing it as another milestone in the state’s ongoing health sector reforms. He said the proposed centre would address the rising incidence of stroke across Africa, particularly Nigeria, by providing specialised facilities for comprehensive treatment and management of neurovascular conditions. According to him, the state government had approved the participation of the Ministry of Health in the international symposium to explore strategic partnerships and opportunities for specialised healthcare development. The Commissioner said Abia’s health sector reforms were also showcased at the symposium, adding that the Ministry of Health had recently been recognised as a national self-care champion. He said the recognition underscored the state’s growing capacity to promote preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles among residents. On public health preparedness, Kanu disclosed that the government had established a multi-sectoral frontline technical working group to strengthen emergency response mechanisms. He said the group had developed an Ebola preparedness and response plan, while the government had expanded the deployment of modern medical technology in specialised healthcare. Kanu further disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital in Aba had been completed, alongside an infectious disease facility and specialist hospital in Umuahia, as part of efforts to strengthen the state’s capacity to tackle Ebola and other infectious diseases. He, however, said no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera or avian influenza were recorded in Abia. The Commissioner also announced progress in the agricultural intervention programme being implemented across the state’s 17 local government areas in partnership with the councils. He said the initiative was designed to attract investments, boost food production, develop viable agricultural enterprises and create employment through strengthened agricultural value chains. The Commissioner disclosed that Arochukwu LGA had a plantation plantation of over 86,000 trees, describing it as highly commendable. item.title: NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment
item.description: By Emmanuel Elebeke The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has intensified its crackdown on illegal National Identification Number (NIN) enrolment, unauthorised data modification and extortion, following an enforcement operation that led to several arrests in Gwagwalada and other locations. The Commission disclosed this in a statement, saying its Inspectorate Compliance and Enforcement Unit (ICEU) carried out the operation and seized equipment allegedly used for illegal enrolment activities. It said the exercise was part of efforts to curb unauthorised enrolment and unethical practices while protecting the integrity, security and credibility of Nigeria’s National Identity Management System. NIMC noted that many of the challenges encountered by NIN holders resulted from attempts to bypass official enrolment procedures. It stressed that NIN enrolment could only be conducted at its approved centres, while requests for modification of personal data could be processed through its self-service modification platform. The Commission also advised NIN holders to download the NINAuth application from the iOS App Store or Google Play Store to access security features, print their NIN slips and enjoy other related services. The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, reiterated the Commission’s zero tolerance for extortion and unethical practices. She said the Commission remained committed to providing seamless and hitch-free NIN enrolment services for Nigerians and legal residents. NIMC urged applicants and existing NIN holders to use only its approved channels for enrolment and other related services. It advised members of the public to visit www.nimc.gov.ng or follow its verified social media platforms for accurate information. item.title: Five officers’ final duty in Zamfara
item.description: From Abdullahi Abdulrahaman Chakwa (Gusau), Salim Umar Ibrahim (Kano) & Dalhatu Liman (Abuja) Five police officers have been killed and several others injured in an ambush by bandits at Gidan Kano on the Gusau-Sokoto highway in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The officers were travelling in an 18-seater bus belonging to the Zamfara State Transport Authority when they were attacked on Monday morning. The security personnel were reportedly on their way to provide security during the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial rerun primary in Zamfara North Senatorial District when the incident occurred. A witness, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the bandits lay in ambush for the security operatives as they travelled along the highway. He said about five officers were feared killed, while several others sustained varying degrees of injury. “The bandits lay in ambush for the security personnel travelling in the Zamfara State Transport Authority bus. Five of them were killed, while many others were injured. The bullets penetrated the bus from different angles,” he said. However, another resident, who also spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, claimed that eight security personnel were killed, while several others were abducted by the gunmen. He said residents helped to evacuate the bodies of the deceased officers but could not account for some of the other personnel. “Eight security personnel were killed, and we helped to load their corpses into two different vehicles. We suspect that the remaining officers were abducted because they could not be found,” he added. In a related development, bandits ambushed workers of a telecommunications company at Tungan Tama village, along the same Gusau-Sokoto highway, a few kilometres from the scene of the attack at Gidan Kano. One person was reportedly killed, while several others sustained injuries in the attack on the telecommunications workers. “The bandits attacked them at Tungan Tama village, but they managed to reach Tashar Mayanchi, where we discovered that one person had been killed,” a resident said. Daily Trust gathered that bandits had carried out several attacks on communities along the highway, targeting travellers, residents and workers. The repeated attacks, involving road blockades, ambushes and kidnappings, have raised concerns about the safety of the strategic highway linking Zamfara State with Sokoto and other parts of the North-West. Commuters using the route continue to face the risk of being caught in attacks, while residents and motorists have expressed fears over the growing insecurity along the corridor. Police confirm attack on officers The spokesperson of the Zone 10 Police Command headquarters in Sokoto, ASP Abdallah Faruk Ambursa, confirmed the attack. The zone covers Kebbi, Sokoto, and Zamfara states. He said the victims were officers attached to the headquarters and were travelling for official duty. He said he could not provide furt

item.title: Open models can do 90% of agentic work at a twentieth of the cost of a frontier LLM: Gartner
item.description: For-profit model-makers, many of which are spending billions on AI infrastructure, will be chasing revenue from just ten percent of steps involved in agentic AI workflows, according to analyst firm Gartner. “Nine in 10 agent workflow steps are routine, and open-weight models handle them at parity for a quarter of the price of the cheapest closed model,” the firm’s senior director Mark Petty and group vice president Raymond Paquet wrote last week in new document titled “Open-Weight Models Will Run 90% of Enterprise Agentic Workflow Steps.” “Typical operational workflows involve hundreds of routine executions, such as classification, tool calling, passing, validating and reconciling data,” the pair observe, before suggesting open-weight models “can handle hundreds of these routine steps for every one that needs frontier reasoning.” “Against the cheapest closed model at the same score, the open model costs a quarter as much. Against a frontier model run on every step, it costs as little as a twentieth,” the pair add. Those are the best-case numbers, because the analysts admit “Current open models can be more verbose and retry more often, so the saving per task against a frontier model is closer to five or six times.” That’s still a lovely saving, but the analysts rate it as the welcome by-product of moving to open models rather than an end in itself. “Years of workflow history are a large part of what an acquirer pays for in a SaaS company and every routine step sent to a frontier API moves a slice of it outside your perimeter,” the pair wrote. “Open-weights preserve your control. The cost saving is a bonus.” The two analysts therefore offer the following strategic planning assumption: “By 2030, 90% of enterprise operational agent workflow steps will execute on open-weight models.” They argue that enterprises will mostly adopt domain-specific open-weight models, because they do well “in scenarios where a small number of highly stable steps run millions of times a month.” Most models, however, are already commodities. Harnesses, the tools that run agents and manage agents, are the source of value in AI products, because one of their roles is to route work to the most appropriate model for a job, without users noticing any impact. A good harness saves money, imposes strong guardrails, and manages agent fleets. Less powerful harnesses leave users with more to do. The paper suggests frontier models will continue to have a role as the engine of research and development and are effectively capital expense. Open-weight models become an operational expense after frontier models do the heavy lifting. ®
